definition_zh: 实施；执行；落实；（软件）部署上线；履行
definition_en: the act or process of putting a plan, policy, system or agreement into actual operation
core_image: 图纸被搬下桌，变成车间里真正转动起来的那条线
scene: 这里指「实施」。 The plan looked simple on paper, but its implementation took two years of retraining.
sceneCN: 这里 implementation 是「计划实施」（第 1 个义项：把方案变成实际运作）；句意：这个计划在纸上看着简单，但实施起来花了两年重新培训。图中可辨识物件：摊开的图纸、卷起的袖口、正在运转的机器、培训名单。

senses.title: Putting a plan into effect
senses.definition: the process of turning an approved plan into real action
senses.definitionCN: 把已获批准的计划转化为实际行动的过程
senses.example: Implementation of the new timetable begins in September.
senses.exampleCN: 新时间表的实施从九月开始。
senses.why: The Latin verb implere means 'to fill up'. A plan is an empty container until implementation fills it with real hours, people and machines.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 implere 意为“填满”。计划在实施之前是个空容器，实施把真实的小时、人和机器填进去。

senses.title: Carrying a policy into practice
senses.definition: the work of applying a law or official policy in daily administration
senses.definitionCN: 在日常行政中适用法律或官方政策的工作
senses.example: Local offices are responsible for policy implementation.
senses.exampleCN: 地方办事处负责政策执行。
senses.why: Here the container is a rule. Implementation is what happens between the text of the rule and the clerk who must apply it.
senses.whyCN: 这里的容器是一条规则。implementation 就是规则文本与必须执行它的办事员之间发生的事。

senses.title: Installing a system in software
senses.definition: in computing, the process of making a designed system run in a real environment
senses.definitionCN: 计算机领域把设计好的系统放入真实环境运行的过程
senses.example: The implementation of the new database took six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 新数据库的部署用了六周。
senses.why: Code that only exists in a design document is still empty. Deployment fills the container with running processes and live users.
senses.whyCN: 只存在于设计文档里的代码仍是空的。部署把容器填进正在运行的进程与真实用户。

senses.title: Performing what was agreed
senses.definition: the carrying out of the duties set down in an agreement or contract
senses.definitionCN: 履行协议或合同中规定的义务
senses.example: The contract's implementation depends on both parties meeting the deadlines.
senses.exampleCN: 合同的履行取决于双方是否按期完成。
senses.why: A signed agreement is a promise shaped like an empty vessel. Implementation is the behaviour that fills it.
senses.whyCN: 签好的协议是一个空器皿形状的承诺。implementation 就是填满它的行为。

senses.title: Turning a method into classroom practice
senses.definition: in education, the translation of a teaching approach into actual lessons
senses.definitionCN: 教育中把教学理念转化为实际课堂的过程
senses.example: Teachers need support during the implementation of the new method.
senses.exampleCN: 教师在新方法落地期间需要支持。
senses.why: A method described in a journal is not yet teaching. The word marks the gap between description and the room full of students.
senses.whyCN: 期刊里描述的方法还不是教学。这个词标记的是描述与那间坐满学生的教室之间的差距。

senses.title: The stage when design becomes operation
senses.definition: in project management, the phase in which the designed solution is built and handed over
senses.definitionCN: 项目管理中构建并交付已设计方案的阶段
senses.example: The project moves from design to implementation in March.
senses.exampleCN: 项目在三月从设计转入实施。
senses.why: Here the word names a stage on a timeline. It is the moment when drawings stop and work begins.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词命名时间轴上的一个阶段。它是图纸停止、工作开始的时刻。

senses.title: The manner in which a measure is applied
senses.definition: the particular way in which a measure is actually carried out
senses.definitionCN: 某项措施实际被执行的具体方式
senses.example: The policy failed because of poor implementation, not bad design.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策失败是因为执行不力，而不是设计不好。
senses.why: The focus shifts from whether to how. Two teams can implement the same rule and produce opposite results.
senses.whyCN: 焦点从“是否”移到“如何”。两个团队可以执行同一条规则，却得到相反结果。

senses.title: The degree to which something is in force
senses.definition: the extent to which a decision has actually been put into effect
senses.definitionCN: 某项决定实际产生效果的程度
senses.example: Full implementation will take another five years.
senses.exampleCN: 全面落实还需要五年。
senses.why: Here the word is measurable. A reform can be 30 percent implemented, which treats the plan as a container filled to a certain level.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词是可测量的。一项改革可以“实施了三成”，这把计划当作一个填到某个高度的容器。

intro.en: Implementation rests on Latin implere, 'to fill up'. The same verb gave English complete, deplete and supply, and its noun implementum first meant 'a filling' before it meant 'a tool'. The modern noun keeps the container image: a plan is filled with action.
intro.cn: implementation 立足拉丁语 implere“填满”。同一动词给出英语 complete、deplete、supply，其名词 implementum 最早意为“填充”，后指“工具”。现代名词保留容器意象：计划被行动填满。

items.en: The root behind plere, 'to fill', is reconstructed as *ple-, and is generally believed to underlie Latin plere, Greek pleres and English full.
items.cn: plere“填满”背后的词根被重构为 *ple-，一般认为是拉丁语 plere、希腊语 pleres 与英语 full 的共同来源。

items.en: Plere meant 'to fill'. With in- it became implere, 'to fill in, to fill up, to fulfil', used of promises as well as vessels.
items.cn: plere 意为“填满”。加 in- 成为 implere“填进去、填满、履行”，既用于容器，也用于承诺。

items.en: Implementum meant 'a filling up' and later 'that which fills, equipment'. How the jump from 'filling' to 'tool' happened is not documented with certainty.
items.cn: implementum 意为“填充”，后指“填充之物、装备”。从“填充”跳到“工具”的具体过程没有确证，来源不确定。

items.en: English implement first meant 'a means of effecting a purpose', then a physical tool. The verb 'to implement' appeared later, in the 19th century.
items.cn: 英语 implement 最早意为“达成目的的手段”，后指实物工具。动词“实施”出现更晚，在 19 世纪。

items.en: Once implement became a verb, implementation named the process. Early examples come from administration and engineering.
items.cn: implement 一旦成为动词，implementation 就命名这一过程。早期用例来自行政与工程领域。

items.en: Software implementation and project implementation made the word a standard term for the gap between design and operation.
items.cn: 软件实施与项目实施使这个词成为“设计与运作之间那段差距”的标准术语。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the verb, the tool and the process noun. The meaning group compares words for carrying something out.
note.cn: 形近组区分动词、工具名词与过程名词；词义组比较“把某事执行下去”的词。

entries.definition: to put a plan or decision into effect. It is the action that the noun names.
entries.definitionCN: 把计划或决定付诸实施。它是名词所命名的动作。

entries.definition: serving as a means to an end. It is rare and belongs to philosophy, not administration.
entries.definitionCN: 作为达成目的之手段的。这个词罕用，属哲学用语，不属行政用语。

entries.definition: the carrying out of a plan, order or legal sentence. It is close to sense 01 but often carries legal or lethal overtones.
entries.definitionCN: 执行计划、命令或法律判决。它接近第 1 义项，但常带法律或处决色彩。

entries.definition: the act of making people obey a law. It is implementation backed by coercion.
entries.definitionCN: 强迫人们遵守法律的行为。它是带强制力的实施。

entries.definition: the placing of resources or software into position for use. It is the technical cousin of sense 03.
entries.definitionCN: 把资源或软件布置到可使用的位置。它是第 3 义项的技术近亲。

entries.definition: the act of making something real or achieving it. It stresses achievement, while implementation stresses the work of building.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事成真或实现。它强调达成，而 implementation 强调建设过程。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build implementation from implere, 'to fill', and let the container image cover plans, policies, software, contracts and classrooms.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩从 implere“填满”搭起 implementation，再用容器意象覆盖计划、政策、软件、合同与课堂。

normal.en: See in- + plere: to fill in. Implementation is a plan being filled with real action.
normal.cn: 看成 in- 加 plere：填进去。implementation 就是计划被真实行动填满。

normal.en: Picture a steel ladle pouring concrete into a mould: the drawing only becomes a building when it is filled.
normal.cn: 想象钢斗把混凝土浇进模具：图纸只有被填满才变成建筑。

normal.en: In software, deployment is the pour: the code finally holds traffic.
normal.cn: 在软件里，部署就是那一浇：代码终于承受真实流量。

normal.en: In a contract, both signatures are the mould; performance is the concrete.
normal.cn: 在合同里，双方签字是模具；履行才是混凝土。

normal.en: Remember the family: complete, deplete and supply all come from the same 'fill' verb.
normal.cn: 记住词族：complete、deplete、supply 都出自同一个“填”的动词。

abstract.en: Keep one image: an empty form waiting for substance, and the risk that it stays empty.
abstract.cn: 只记一个意象：一张空表格等待内容，以及它可能一直空着的风险。

abstract.en: Treat the word as the answer to 'who actually does it, with what, starting when?'
abstract.cn: 把这个词当作对“谁真正去做、用什么做、从何时开始”的回答。

abstract.en: Notice that failure usually happens here, not in the design room.
abstract.cn: 注意失败通常发生在这里，而不是在设计室里。

examples.en: The implementation of the peace agreement is behind schedule.
examples.cn: 和平协议的实施落后于计划。

examples.en: Good policy is useless without competent implementation.
examples.cn: 没有得力的执行，好政策也无用。

examples.en: The software implementation required a full system migration.
examples.cn: 这次软件实施需要完整的系统迁移。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“硬不累门太深”：再硬的任务也不嫌累，门槛太深也要钻进去把事办成——这就是实施。

root: 拉丁语 implere“填满、履行”（in- 进入 + plere 填满），名词 implementum 原指“填充”，后转指“工具、器具”；implement 作动词后加 -ation 构成 implementation。

sensesIntro.en: Implementation is the moment a document stops being a document. A plan, a policy, a database, a contract, a teaching method, a project phase, a style of carrying out and a percentage completed are all versions of one act: filling an empty form with real work. The eight senses differ in what the container is and how full it has become.
sensesIntro.cn: implementation 是文件不再是文件的那一刻。计划、政策、数据库、合同、教学方法、项目阶段、执行方式、完成百分比，都是同一个动作的版本：用真实工作填满一张空表格。八个义项的差别在于容器是什么、已经填到多满。

core.en: Filling a designed form with real action until it works.
core.cn: 用真实行动填满设计好的形式，直到它运转起来。

branches.en: PROJECT: a plan leaves the drawing board and becomes a phase of work.
branches.cn: 项目：计划离开图板，成为一段施工阶段。

branches.en: ADMINISTRATION: a rule is applied, and the manner of applying decides the result.
branches.cn: 行政：规则被适用，而适用方式决定结果。

branches.en: SYSTEMS: designed code is placed in a live environment.
branches.cn: 系统：设计好的代码被放入真实环境。

branches.en: OBLIGATION: promised duties are actually performed.
branches.cn: 义务：承诺的义务被真正履行。

branches.en: PRACTICE: a method reaches the classroom, and coverage can be measured.
branches.cn: 实践：方法抵达课堂，覆盖程度可被测量。

intro.en: Implementation is implement plus -ation. The items below gather the 'fill' family and show how the same Latin verb yields words for completeness, emptiness and supply.
intro.cn: implementation 是 implement 加 -ation。下列条目汇总“填”的词族，并展示同一拉丁动词如何造出表示完整、空竭与供给的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the verb, its root and the noun that shifted from 'filling' to 'tool'. That shift explains the double life of English implement.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出动词、其词根，以及从“填充”转向“工具”的名词。这次转变解释了英语 implement 的双重身份。

items.example: They completed the survey in a week.

items.example: The archive is replete with letters.

items.example: A vitamin supplement filled the gap in her diet.

definition_en: a large basin formed when a volcano collapses or erupts and empties its magma chamber
core_image: 山顶塌下去，留下一个能装下整座城镇的圆坑
scene: 火山塌陷后留下一个宽到能装下整座城的圆坑。 The caldera is so wide that the whole town sits inside it.

senses.definition: a wide depression left when a volcano empties and its roof falls in
senses.definitionCN: 火山喷空后顶部塌落形成的大片洼地
senses.example: The caldera filled with rain and became a lake.
senses.exampleCN: 破火山口积雨成湖。
senses.why: Spanish caldera means a cauldron, which the shape resembles.
senses.whyCN: 西班牙语 caldera 意为大锅，形状正如一口锅。

senses.title: The whole volcanic structure
senses.definition: the volcano and its collapsed centre considered together
senses.definitionCN: 把火山与塌陷的中心合起来看
senses.example: Scientists mapped the whole caldera from the air.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家从空中测绘整个火山结构。
senses.why: Geologists extend the word from the hollow to the feature that contains it.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把这个词从凹陷扩展到包含它的整体。

intro.en: Caldera is Spanish for a cauldron, borrowed into geology for its shape.
intro.cn: caldera 在西班牙语中意为大锅，地质学因其形状而借用。

items.en: Caldaria means a vessel for hot water.

items.en: Caldera means a cauldron.

items.en: Caldera names the basin and the volcano.

entries.definitionCN: 火山口。

abstract.en: A lake sitting in an old explosion.

definition_zh: adj. 仓促的；草率的；粗略的
definition_en: done quickly and without attention to detail
core_image: 目光像跑者一样掠过纸面，一个字也没停下
scene: 他只草草看了一眼报告就签了字。 He gave the report a cursory glance and signed it.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：cursory 指草率一瞥的；句意是他草草看了一眼报告就签了字。

senses.title: Quick and shallow
senses.definition: looking or reading fast without taking it in
senses.definitionCN: 看得快却没看进去
senses.example: A cursory glance missed the typo.
senses.exampleCN: 草草一瞥漏掉了那个错字。
senses.why: Eyes running over a page.
senses.whyCN: 目光跑过一页纸。

senses.title: Done as a formality
senses.definition: performed only because the rules demand it
senses.definitionCN: 只因规定要求才做一遍
senses.example: The safety check was cursory at best.
senses.exampleCN: 那次安全检查充其量只是走个形式。
senses.why: A stamp pressed without reading.
senses.whyCN: 没读就盖下的章。

senses.title: Brief in passing
senses.definition: short and made while moving on to something else
senses.definitionCN: 简短且边走边做
senses.example: He made a cursory note of the address.
senses.exampleCN: 他顺手粗略记下了地址。
senses.why: A signature written on a moving train.
senses.whyCN: 在行进列车上写下的签名。

intro.en: Cursory comes from Latin cursorius, of a runner, hence running past the details.
intro.cn: cursory 源自拉丁语 cursorius（奔跑者的），因此是跑着掠过细节。

items.en: Currere meant to run.
items.cn: currere 意为跑。

items.en: Cursorius meant belonging to a runner.
items.cn: cursorius 意为属于奔跑者的。

items.en: The word came to mean hasty.
items.cn: 这个词后来表示仓促。

items.en: Cursory described hurried, careless work.
items.cn: 十七世纪 cursory 形容匆忙马虎的工作。

items.en: Cursory became common in reports and audits.
items.cn: 二十世纪 cursory 常见于报告与审计。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the running root; the near-meaning group names shallow, hurried work.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示跑的词根；近义组都是浅而快的工作。

definition_zh: 考古记录；物质遗存总体；发掘与登记档案
definition_en: the surviving body of material remains and the documentation of excavations, taken together as the record of the human past
core_image: 一面墙的架子上排满纸盒，每盒贴一个编号，旁边是一排写满层位与坐标的登记册
scene: 库房的架子上排满纸盒，每盒贴一个编号，旁边一摞登记册写满层位与坐标。 The archaeological record fills the shelves with numbered boxes and matching registers.
sceneCN: 这里 archaeological record 指「留存下来的物质遗存与发掘记录合在一起构成的总体」（第 1 个义项：作为人类过去之记录的物质与文献总和）；句意为架上的编号纸盒与对应登记册共同构成这份记录。可辨识物件：纸盒、编号签、登记册、铅笔、层位表。

pos.zh: 考古记录；物质遗存总体（不可数）
（某一地区或某次发掘的）记录材料

senses.title: The surviving material record
senses.titleCN: 物质遗存总体：留存下来的全部物质材料
senses.definition: everything that survives from past human activity and can be studied as a body of material
senses.definitionCN: 过去人类活动中留存下来、可作为材料总体研究的一切
senses.example: Forests and cities both leave different traces in the archaeological record.
senses.exampleCN: 森林与城市在考古记录中留下不同的痕迹。
senses.why: Record comes from Latin recordari, to remember, built on cor, heart: the word treats matter as a memory that the earth kept.
senses.whyCN: record 出自拉丁 recordari「记住」，其词根是 cor「心」：这个词把物质当作大地保存下来的记忆。

senses.title: The field documentation
senses.titleCN: 田野记录：发掘现场的表格与笔记
senses.definition: the notes, plans, sections and photographs made while a site is being dug
senses.definitionCN: 发掘过程中所做的笔记、平面图、剖面图与照片
senses.example: The archaeological record for the trench fills four notebooks.
senses.exampleCN: 这个探方的田野记录写满了四个笔记本。
senses.why: Digging destroys the deposit, so the written record must replace what the spade removes; documentation is the site's second life.
senses.whyCN: 发掘会毁掉堆积，因此文字记录必须替代铁锹移走的东西；档案就是遗址的第二次生命。

senses.title: The published literature
senses.titleCN: 已发表记录：正式出版的研究材料
senses.definition: the published reports and articles through which a dig becomes available to other researchers
senses.definitionCN: 使一次发掘可为其他研究者使用的正式报告与论文
senses.example: Much of the archaeological record is known only through old reports.
senses.exampleCN: 考古记录的很大部分只能通过旧报告得知。
senses.why: An unpublished dig is nearly invisible; publication is what turns private notes into a public record.
senses.whyCN: 未发表的发掘几乎不可见；出版才把私人笔记变成公共记录。

senses.title: The register and database
senses.titleCN: 登记册与数据库：编目化的记录
senses.definition: the catalogued list of sites, finds and contexts held in a register or database
senses.definitionCN: 以登记册或数据库形式保存的地点、发现物与情境目录
senses.example: The national archaeological record lists every known burial mound.
senses.exampleCN: 全国考古记录列出了每一处已知的墓葬土丘。
senses.why: Once entries are numbered and indexed, the record becomes searchable, and a searchable past is a different kind of evidence.
senses.whyCN: 一旦条目被编号并建立索引，记录就变得可检索，而可检索的过去是另一种证据。

senses.title: The regional sequence
senses.titleCN: 区域序列：某地区遗存的年代序列
senses.definition: the ordered succession of material from one region, used to place finds in time
senses.definitionCN: 某地区材料的先后序列，用于把发现物定位到时间中
senses.example: The island's archaeological record runs from early farming to the bronze age.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的考古记录从早期农耕延续到青铜时代。
senses.why: Materials from one area accumulate into a sequence, and that sequence becomes the local ruler against which new finds are measured.
senses.whyCN: 同一地区的材料累积成序列，这个序列就成为衡量新发现的地方标尺。

senses.title: Bias and incompleteness
senses.titleCN: 偏差与不完整：记录本身的偏向
senses.definition: the distortion in the record caused by what survives, what is found and what is published
senses.definitionCN: 因何物留存、何物被发现、何物被发表而造成的记录偏差
senses.example: Stone survives better, so the archaeological record overstates stone tools.
senses.exampleCN: 石头更易保存，因此考古记录夸大了石器的比重。
senses.why: The record is a sample, not a census: decay, discovery and publication each filter it, and every filter leaves a bias.
senses.whyCN: 记录是样本而非普查：腐朽、发现与发表各是一道筛子，每道筛子都留下偏差。

senses.title: Curation of the archive
senses.titleCN: 档案保存：记录被长期维护的状态
senses.definition: the state of being kept, conserved and made accessible in a museum or archive
senses.definitionCN: 在博物馆或档案馆中被保存、修复并可查阅的状态
senses.example: Poor curation has already damaged part of the archaeological record.
senses.exampleCN: 保存不善已经损坏了部分考古记录。
senses.why: Documentation and objects decay too, so the record needs care; curation is what keeps a past record from becoming a future loss.
senses.whyCN: 档案与物件也会衰败，因此记录需要照料；保存工作防止过去的记录变成未来的损失。

senses.title: The record as a research archive
senses.titleCN: 作为研究资料库的记录
senses.definition: the accumulated body of material and data reused for new questions long after the original dig
senses.definitionCN: 原始发掘结束很久之后，仍被用于新问题的材料与数据总体
senses.example: Old samples in the archaeological record answered a new question about diet.
senses.exampleCN: 考古记录中的旧样本回答了一个关于饮食的新问题。
senses.why: Good records outlive their questions; the archive becomes a mine that later researchers can reopen with new tools.
senses.whyCN: 好的记录比它最初的问题活得更久；资料库成为后来者可用新工具重开的矿。

intro.en: Archaeological record joins Greek archaeology, the study of ancient things, with record, from Latin recordari, to remember. The phrase treats material and documents as one memory of the past. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: archaeological record 把希腊来源的 archaeology（研究古代事物）与 record 连在一起；record 出自拉丁 recordari「记住」。这个短语把物质与文献当成同一份关于过去的记忆。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cor, genitive cordis, meant heart, and the Romans placed memory in the heart; recordari meant to remember, literally to bring back to the heart.
items.cn: cor（属格 cordis）意为心，罗马人把记忆安置在心里；recordari 意为记住，字面是「重新带回心里」。

items.en: Recordari, built on re-, back, plus cor, produced recorder in Old French and record in English, first as a verb and then as a noun.
items.cn: recordari 由 re-「回」加 cor 构成，经古法语 recorder 产生英语 record，先作动词，后作名词。

items.en: Arkhaios, ancient, plus logos, account, gave the name of the discipline that studies material remains.
items.cn: arkhaios「古老」加 logos「叙述」，构成研究物质遗存之学科的名称。

items.en: Nineteenth-century archaeologists began to speak of a record because the surviving material could be read like an archive, with entries, gaps and losses.
items.cn: 十九世纪考古学者开始谈「记录」，因为留存材料可以像档案一样阅读，有条目、空缺与散失。

items.en: Source uncertain: the date at which the phrase became standard is not documented, and the metaphor of material as a record has been criticised as misleading by later scholars.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个短语成为标准说法的年代没有文献记载，而把物质比作记录的做法后来也受到学者批评，认为会误导。

note.en: The first group holds phrases that name parts or views of the same archive; the second group holds words for bodies of stored information.
note.cn: 第一组是命名同一档案之部分或视角的短语；第二组是表示储存信息总体的词。

entries.definition: The portion of the record used to support one specific claim; the record is the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 记录中用于支持某一具体论断的部分；记录是整体。

entries.definition: The systematic search that adds new entries to the record rather than the record itself.
entries.definitionCN: 为记录增添新条目的系统搜寻，而非记录本身。

entries.definition: The documentation for a single site, a small unit inside the larger record.
entries.definitionCN: 单个遗址的档案，是更大记录中的一个小编单位。

entries.definition: An organised store of documents; the archaeological record includes objects as well as documents.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的文献储存；考古记录除文献外还包括实物。

entries.definition: A structured set of searchable entries; it is one modern form of the record, not its whole content.
entries.definitionCN: 可检索条目的结构化集合；它是记录的现代形式之一，而非全部内容。

entries.definition: Evidence given by a witness; it is human speech, while the archaeological record is mostly mute matter.
entries.definitionCN: 证人提供的证据；它出自人的言说，而考古记录多半是无声的物质。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the heart-rooted memory word, the Greek discipline, the filters of decay and the archive that outlives its dig.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：以「心」为根的记忆词、希腊学科、腐朽造成的筛子，以及比发掘活得更久的档案。

normal.en: recordari, to remember, from cor, heart: the record is the earth's memory.
normal.cn: recordari「记住」出自 cor「心」：记录就是大地的记忆。

normal.en: Archaeology is the Greek account of ancient things, and the record is what that account is built on.
normal.cn: archaeology 是希腊语「关于古代事物的叙述」，记录正是这项叙述的立足处。

normal.en: Digging destroys, so the written record must stand in for what the spade removed.
normal.cn: 发掘会毁坏，因此文字记录必须代替铁锹移走的部分。

normal.en: Three filters shape it: what survives, what is found, what is published.
normal.cn: 三道筛子塑造它：什么留存下来、什么被发现、什么被发表。

normal.en: A good archive outlives its original question and can be reopened later.
normal.cn: 好的档案比它最初的问题活得更久，日后还能被重新打开。

abstract.en: Abstractly, a record is a sample pretending to be a census, and its gaps are as informative as its entries.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，记录是伪装成普查的样本，它的空缺与条目同样有信息量。

abstract.en: The word fuses matter and memory: what is kept is at once an object and a statement.
abstract.cn: 这个词把物质与记忆熔在一起：被保存的东西既是物件，也是陈述。

abstract.en: Every archive decides what the future will be able to ask.
abstract.cn: 每座档案库都在决定未来能提出什么问题。

examples.en: Coastal sites are poorly represented in the archaeological record.
examples.cn: 海岸遗址在考古记录中所占比例很低。

examples.en: The excavation was never published, so it barely enters the archaeological record.
examples.cn: 这次发掘从未发表，因此几乎未进入考古记录。

examples.en: New dating methods let researchers re-read the same archaeological record.
examples.cn: 新的测年方法让研究者重读同一份考古记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「考古（archaeology）+ 记录（record）」——埋在地下、又被写进册子的全部痕迹 → 考古记录

root: 希腊 arkhaios「古老的」+ logos「叙述」构成 archaeology；拉丁 recordari「记住」（re- + cor「心」）构成 record；字面为「关于古代遗存的记忆总体」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one archive: matter survives, diggers write it down, reports publish it, registers index it, regions order it, filters bias it, curators keep it and later researchers reopen it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一座档案库展开：物质留存，发掘者记下，报告发表，登记册编目，区域排序，筛子造成偏差，保管者维护，后来者重开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: numbered boxes on a shelf beside registers that describe them.
core.cn: 核心意象：架上的编号纸盒，旁边是描述它们的登记册。

branches.en: MATTER AND ORDER: the surviving body gains meaning only when arranged into a regional sequence.
branches.cn: 物质与秩序：留存总体只有排成区域序列才获得意义。

branches.en: WRITING REPLACES DIGGING: notes and reports preserve what the spade destroyed.
branches.cn: 书写替代挖掘：笔记与报告保存了铁锹毁掉的东西。

branches.en: THE INDEX: numbering turns a heap into a searchable record.
branches.cn: 索引：编号把一堆东西变成可检索的记录。

branches.en: THE FILTERS: decay, discovery and publication bias the sample, and care is needed to keep what remains.
branches.cn: 筛子：腐朽、发现与发表使样本带偏，而留存部分需要照料。

branches.en: THE REOPENED MINE: an archive outlives its questions and serves new ones.
branches.cn: 重开的矿：档案比它的问题活得更久，并服务于新问题。

intro.en: Archaeological record is a Greek-Latin hybrid phrase: the discipline from Greek and the memory word from Latin.
intro.cn: archaeological record 是一个希腊—拉丁混合短语：学科名来自希腊语，记忆之词来自拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: Greek arkhaios and logos build archaeology; Latin re- and cor build record, recordari and recorder. English record then extends to recording, recorded and recordation.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 arkhaios 与 logos 构成 archaeology；拉丁 re- 与 cor 构成 record、recordari、recorder。英语 record 再扩展出 recording、recorded、recordation。

items.example: Arkhaios marks what belongs to an early age.
items.exampleCN: arkhaios 标记属于早期时代之物。
考古学依赖细致的记录。

items.example: Cor is the root of record and cordial.
items.exampleCN: cor 是 record 与 cordial 的词根。

items.meaning: to remember, to call back to mind
items.example: Recordari is the source of English record.
items.exampleCN: recordari 是英语 record 的来源。

items.meaning: to set down, or a written account
items.example: Every find is recorded with coordinates.
items.exampleCN: 每件发现物都连坐标一起记录。

items.meaning: the act or product of setting down
items.example: Good recording saves a site from oblivion.
items.exampleCN: 良好的记录使遗址免于湮没。

items.meaning: set down in writing or data
items.example: The wall is recorded in plan and section.
items.exampleCN: 这堵墙被记录在平面图与剖面图中。

items.example: The recorder noted the depth of each layer.
items.exampleCN: 记录员记下每一层的深度。

items.example: Recordation of the find took a full day.
items.exampleCN: 这件发现物的登记记录花了一整天。

definition_zh: 认知心理学：研究知觉、记忆、注意、语言与推理等心智过程的心理学分支，常以信息加工模型解释心智
definition_en: the branch of psychology that studies perception, memory, attention, language and reasoning, often modelling the mind as information processing
core_image: 一串字符先落在视网膜上，被切成片段、贴上标签、存进记忆抽屉，最后从口中重新拼成一句话
scene: 一串字符先落在视网膜上，被切成片段、贴上标签、存进记忆抽屉，最后从口中重新拼成一句话。 Modern cognitive psychology treats that route as a set of testable stages.
sceneCN: 这里指研究知觉、记忆、语言等心智过程的学科分支（第 1 个义项：认知心理学作为学科）；句意为现代认知心理学把这条路线当作一组可检验的阶段。

pos.zh: 认知心理学（不可数，学科分支名）

collocations.zh: 记忆的认知心理学研究

derivatives.zh: cognitio + -ion（动作或结果）→ 认知这一过程或其能力
cognitus + -ive（具有……性质的）→ 具有认知性质的
cognitive + -ly（方式副词）→ 从认知层面
cognitive + -ism（学说）→ 以内部表征解释行为的立场
meta-（超越） + cognition → 对自身认知过程的认知

senses.title: The branch that studies mental processes
senses.titleCN: 研究心智过程的心理学分支
senses.definition: the branch of psychology that studies perception, attention, memory, language, reasoning and problem solving
senses.definitionCN: 研究知觉、注意、记忆、语言、推理与问题解决的心理学分支
senses.example: Cognitive psychology asks how a sentence is understood in real time.
senses.exampleCN: 认知心理学追问一句话是如何被实时理解的。
senses.why: cognitive marks mental processes and psychology marks the discipline, so the phrase names the branch that studies those processes.
senses.whyCN: cognitive 标记心智过程，psychology 标记学科，短语因此指研究这些过程的分支。

senses.title: The information-processing stance
senses.definition: the approach that describes the mind as a system that encodes, stores and retrieves information
senses.definitionCN: 把心智描述为编码、存储与提取信息的系统的取向
senses.example: The information-processing stance gave memory a measurable architecture.
senses.exampleCN: 信息加工取向给了记忆一个可测量的结构。
senses.why: the branch needed a model that could be tested stage by stage, and the computer supplied one.
senses.whyCN: 这个分支需要一个能逐阶段检验的模型，计算机提供了这个模型。

senses.title: The study of perception and attention
senses.definition: the part of the field that asks how sensory input is selected, grouped and recognised
senses.definitionCN: 研究感官输入如何被选择、分组与识别的那部分
senses.example: Cognitive psychology showed that attention filters before recognition.
senses.exampleCN: 认知心理学表明注意在识别之前就进行筛选。
senses.why: before anything can be remembered it must be selected, so perception and attention sit at the entrance of the model.
senses.whyCN: 任何东西在被记住之前必须先被选中，因此知觉与注意位于模型的入口。

senses.title: The study of memory
senses.definition: the study of encoding, storage, forgetting and retrieval, including working and long-term memory
senses.definitionCN: 研究编码、存储、遗忘与提取，包括工作记忆与长时记忆
senses.example: Cognitive psychology split working memory into separate stores.
senses.exampleCN: 认知心理学把工作记忆拆成几个独立的存储。
senses.why: a processing model needs a place to put information, and memory is that place.
senses.whyCN: 加工模型需要一个存放信息的地方，记忆就是那个地方。

senses.title: The study of language processing
senses.definition: the study of how sounds, words and sentences are recognised and produced in real time
senses.definitionCN: 研究语音、词与句子如何被实时识别与产出
senses.example: Cognitive psychology mapped the moment a listener resolves an ambiguous word.
senses.exampleCN: 认知心理学标出了听者解决歧义词的那一刻。
senses.why: language is the most finely timed mental skill, so it became a test case for the whole model.
senses.whyCN: 语言是时间精度最高的心智技能，因此成为整个模型的试验案例。

senses.title: The study of reasoning and decision
senses.definition: the study of how people draw inferences, weigh options and fall into systematic errors
senses.definitionCN: 研究人如何推断、权衡选项并落入系统性错误
senses.example: Cognitive psychology documented the bias that survives formal training.
senses.exampleCN: 认知心理学记录了经受正式训练仍存活的偏见。
senses.why: if perception and memory can be modelled, the same stage logic can be turned toward judgement.
senses.whyCN: 如果知觉与记忆可以被建模，同样的阶段逻辑也能转向判断。

senses.title: Cognitive load and learning design
senses.definition: the application of memory limits to the design of explanations, texts and interfaces for learners
senses.definitionCN: 把记忆容量限制用于学习者所用的讲解、文本与界面设计
senses.example: Cognitive psychology persuaded the textbook to remove decorative diagrams.
senses.exampleCN: 认知心理学说服教材删掉了装饰性图表。
senses.why: once working memory has a limit, teaching can be designed to stay under it.
senses.whyCN: 工作记忆一旦有了上限，教学就能被设计得不越过这个上限。

senses.title: Human-computer interaction
senses.definition: the use of attention, memory and motor limits to evaluate screens, menus and response times
senses.definitionCN: 用注意、记忆与动作限制评估屏幕、菜单与响应时间
senses.example: Cognitive psychology explained why the third menu level lost every user.
senses.exampleCN: 认知心理学解释了为什么第三层菜单让所有用户迷路。
senses.why: an interface is a stream of stimuli, so the branch's measurements transfer directly to design.
senses.whyCN: 界面是一串刺激流，因此这个分支的测量可直接转移到设计上。

senses.title: Its place within cognitive science
senses.definition: the psychological member of the wider cognitive science group, alongside linguistics, computer science and neuroscience
senses.definitionCN: 更宽的认知科学群体中的心理学成员，与语言学、计算机科学和神经科学并列
senses.example: Cognitive psychology shares its questions with cognitive science but keeps behaviour as its test.
senses.exampleCN: 认知心理学与认知科学共享问题，但以行为作为检验。
senses.why: the branch is narrower than the whole field, since it keeps psychology's methods while sharing the field's questions.
senses.whyCN: 这个分支比整个领域窄，因为它保留心理学的方法，却共享领域的问题。

intro.en: Cognitive psychology joins a Latin adjective with a Greek-derived discipline name. Cognitive goes back to Latin cognoscere 'to get to know'; psychology goes back to Greek psykhe and logos. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cognitive psychology 由拉丁形容词与希腊来源的学科名组合而成。cognitive 追溯至拉丁 cognoscere「认识、得知」；psychology 追溯至希腊 psykhe 与 logos。年代为约数。

items.en: Cognoscere 'to get to know, to recognise' was built from com- 'together, fully' and gnoscere 'to know', a variant of noscere.
items.cn: cognoscere「认识、得知」由 com-「共同、彻底」与 gnoscere「知道」构成，gnoscere 是 noscere 的变体。

items.en: The noun cognitio meant 'a getting to know, knowledge, recognition', and the Late Latin adjective cognitivus meant 'relating to knowledge'.
items.cn: 名词 cognitio 意为「认识、知识、识别」，晚期拉丁形容词 cognitivus 意为「与知识有关的」。

items.en: Psychology joins psykhe 'breath, life, soul' with logos 'account, reason'; -logia named the study of a subject.
items.cn: psychology 把 psykhe「气息、生命、灵魂」与 logos「论述、理性」结合起来；-logia 命名对某一主题的研究。

items.en: Cognitive entered English in the seventeenth century from Latin cognitivus, first as a philosophical word for knowledge and recognition.
items.cn: cognitive 在 17 世纪从拉丁 cognitivus 进入英语，最初是哲学术语，指知识与识别。

items.en: From the 1950s and 1960s the phrase cognitive psychology named the approach that studied internal processing with behavioural tests, in reaction against behaviorism.
items.cn: 从 1950 至 1960 年代起，cognitive psychology 指用行为检验研究内部加工的取向，是对行为主义的反弹。

items.en: Source uncertain (first use of the exact phrase): the label spread through conferences and textbooks in the 1960s and 1970s, so no single first citation is settled; the link of gnoscere to the Indo-European root for 'know' is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（确切短语的首见）：这个标签在 1960 至 1970 年代经会议与教科书扩散，没有公认的首次书证；gnoscere 与印欧语「知道」词根的联系属重构。

note.en: Group one holds neighbouring labels built on cognitive that cover different scopes; group two holds disciplines that study the same questions with different tools.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 cognitive、覆盖范围不同的邻近标签；第二组是用不同工具研究同一批问题的学科。

entries.definition: The interdisciplinary field covering psychology, linguistics, artificial intelligence, philosophy and neuroscience; cognitive psychology is one member.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖心理学、语言学、人工智能、哲学与神经科学的交叉领域，认知心理学只是其中一员。

entries.definition: The study of cognitive processes through brain imaging and physiology rather than through behaviour alone.
entries.definitionCN: 通过脑成像与生理指标而非仅靠行为来研究认知过程。

entries.definition: A theoretical position that explains behaviour through internal representations; it can appear inside several disciplines.
entries.definitionCN: 以内部表征解释行为的理论立场，可以出现在多个学科内部。

entries.definition: The study of how brain structure and damage affect behaviour and cognition; it starts from the organ.
entries.definitionCN: 研究脑结构与损伤如何影响行为与认知，出发点是有机体器官。

entries.definition: The study of language as a mental process; it overlaps with cognitive psychology but is confined to language.
entries.definitionCN: 把语言作为心理过程来研究，与认知心理学重叠，但范围限于语言。

entries.definition: The specific model of encoding, storage and retrieval; it is a framework used by the field rather than the field itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指编码、存储、提取这一具体模型，是领域使用的框架，而非领域本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real model names and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实模型名与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: com- 'fully' plus gnoscere 'know': cognition is a full getting-to-know.
normal.cn: com-「彻底」加 gnoscere「知道」：认知就是彻底地认识。

normal.en: The family runs cognition, cognitive, cognitively, cognitivism, metacognition.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cognition、cognitive、cognitively、cognitivism、metacognition。

normal.en: The second half is the same psychology seen in clinical and school psychology.
normal.cn: 后半部分就是临床与学校心理学中见到的同一个 psychology。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: cognitive psychology of memory, cognitive psychology experiments.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：记忆的认知心理学、认知心理学实验。

normal.en: Its rival in the twentieth century was behaviorism, which refused to model the inner stage.
normal.cn: 它在 20 世纪的对手是行为主义，后者拒绝为内部阶段建模。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence entering the eye and leaving the mouth as a rebuilt copy.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话从眼睛进入，又从口中作为重建的副本出来。

abstract.en: Picture a mind drawn as boxes joined by arrows, with a clock beside each arrow.
abstract.cn: 想象心智被画成方框与箭头，每个箭头旁都有一只钟。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer labelled 'words' that opens only when the right cue arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象一只标着「词」的抽屉，只在正确提示到来时打开。

examples.en: Cognitive psychology replaced the black box with a stage model.
examples.cn: 认知心理学用阶段模型取代了黑箱。

examples.en: Her thesis applied cognitive psychology to menu design.
examples.cn: 她的论文把认知心理学应用于菜单设计。

examples.en: Cognitive psychology and neuroscience now share most of their methods.
examples.cn: 认知心理学与神经科学如今共享大部分方法。

dict_mnemonic.text: cognitive（认知的）+ psychology（心理学）＝ 认知心理学；记「字符进眼、切块贴签、入抽屉、再出口」。

root: 拉丁 com-「共同、彻底」+ gnoscere「知道」（noscere 的变体）→ cognoscere「认识」，其形容词 cognitivus；加希腊 psykhe「灵魂」+ logos「论述」。短语在 20 世纪中叶定型。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one stream of information: it enters as sensory input, is selected, stored, retrieved, used in language and judgement, then designed for in classrooms and on screens.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿着同一股信息流展开：它作为感官输入进入，被选择、存储、提取，用于语言与判断，最后在课堂与屏幕上被设计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a string of characters entering the eye, broken into pieces, filed in drawers, and rebuilt into speech.
core.cn: 核心意象：一串字符进入眼睛，被切成片段、归档进抽屉，再被重建成言语。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the phrase names the branch that studies these stages as a whole.
branches.cn: 领域：短语指整体研究这些阶段的学科分支。

branches.en: THE MODEL AND THE GATE: information processing supplies the architecture, and attention guards its entrance.
branches.cn: 模型与入口：信息加工提供结构，注意守着入口。

branches.en: TWO STORES: memory holds what is kept, and language shows it being taken out and reassembled.
branches.cn: 两个仓库：记忆保存被留下的东西，语言则展示它被取出并重新组装。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT AND TEACHING: the same stages explain bias and set the limits for instruction.
branches.cn: 判断与教学：同一套阶段既解释偏见，也为教学设定上限。

branches.en: SCREENS AND THE WIDER FIELD: the model moves into interface design and sits beside linguistics and neuroscience.
branches.cn: 屏幕与更宽的领域：模型进入界面设计，并与语言学和神经科学并列。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Latin-derived adjective with a Greek-derived discipline name, so both a Latin root and a Greek root can be read inside it.
intro.cn: 这个短语由拉丁来源的形容词与希腊来源的学科名组合，因此其中可读出拉丁词根与希腊词根各一。

latinIntro.en: Latin cognoscere, cognitio and cognitivus supply the first word; Greek psykhe, logos and -logia supply the second.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cognoscere、cognitio 与 cognitivus 提供第一个词；希腊 psykhe、logos 与 -logia 提供第二个词。

items.example: The prefix intensifies the act of knowing.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀强化「知道」这一动作。

items.structure: gnoscere (Latin verb variant of noscere, 'to know')
items.example: The root also gives notice and notion.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根还给出 notice 与 notion。

items.meaning: to get to know, to recognise
items.example: The verb stresses a completed act of knowing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词强调认识动作的完成。

items.example: The noun names both the act and its result.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既指动作，也指结果。

items.example: The adjective reached English as cognitive.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词进入英语成为 cognitive。

items.example: It supplies the first element of psychology.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 psychology 的第一个成分。

items.example: It supplies the second element of psychology.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 psychology 的第二个成分。

items.example: The suffix appears in biology and geology.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀出现在 biology 与 geology 中。

items.example: The adjective marks the mental side of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标记短语中属于心智的一面。

latinEntries.meaning: to get to know, recognise, learn

definition_zh: 证券；可交易的金融工具（股票、债券等）
definition_en: tradable financial instruments, such as shares and bonds
core_image: 一叠盖着印章的凭证，每一张都能在市场上换成钱
scene: 听证会上，监管人员指出这家公司向公众出售可交易的投资凭证时没有充分披露风险。 The regulator accused the firm of selling securities without proper disclosure.
sceneCN: 这里指「可交易的金融工具」，对应第 1 个义项：股票、债券等可在市场上买卖的凭证；句意为监管者指控该公司出售证券时未充分披露信息。画面要点：成叠凭证、监管徽章、披露文件。

pos.zh: 证券（复数形式，统指股票、债券等可交易金融工具）

derivatives.zh: 安全；保障；单数形式的证券

senses.title: Tradable financial instruments as a class
senses.titleCN: 作为一类可交易金融工具
senses.definition: financial instruments that can be bought and sold in markets, such as shares and bonds
senses.definitionCN: 可在市场上买卖的金融工具，如股票与债券
senses.example: Banks must hold enough capital against their securities.
senses.exampleCN: 银行必须为其证券持有足够的资本。
senses.why: The plural of security names instruments that make an investor feel secure because they can be sold or redeemed; the abstract assurance becomes a countable paper claim.
senses.whyCN: security 的复数指那些因可出售或可兑付而让投资者安心的工具；抽象的保障于是变成可计数的纸面权利。

senses.title: Debt securities
senses.definition: instruments that represent a loan to an issuer, such as bonds and notes
senses.definitionCN: 代表向发行人提供贷款的工具，如债券与票据
senses.example: The fund shifted from shares into debt securities.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金从股票转向债务证券。
senses.why: One branch of the class is pure borrowing: the holder has lent money and holds a right to interest and repayment.
senses.whyCN: 这一类中的一支是纯粹的借贷：持有人借出了资金，握有收取利息与收回本金的权利。

senses.title: Equity securities
senses.definition: instruments that represent ownership in a company, such as shares
senses.definitionCN: 代表公司所有权的工具，如股票
senses.example: Equity securities carry voting rights and dividend claims.
senses.exampleCN: 权益证券带有表决权与股息主张。
senses.why: The other branch is ownership rather than lending: the holder owns a portion of the company and shares in its fortunes.
senses.whyCN: 另一支是所有权而非借贷：持有人拥有公司的一部分，并与其命运与共。

senses.title: Government securities
senses.definition: debt instruments issued by a government or its agencies
senses.definitionCN: 由政府或其机构发行的债务工具
senses.example: During the crisis investors rushed into government securities.
senses.exampleCN: 危机期间投资者涌向政府证券。
senses.why: The class is narrowed by the issuer: the same instrument is backed by the taxing power of a state rather than by a company.
senses.whyCN: 这一类按发行人收窄：同样的工具由国家征税能力而非公司信用支撑。

senses.title: Certificates of ownership
senses.definition: documents that evidence a right to a share or an asset
senses.definitionCN: 证明对股份或资产享有权利的文件
senses.example: The old certificates were replaced by electronic securities.
senses.exampleCN: 旧式纸质凭证被电子证券取代。
senses.why: Before computers the security was a physical paper that proved the claim, which is the literal root of the financial sense.
senses.whyCN: 在计算机之前，证券就是证明权利的一纸实物，这正是金融义的字面来源。

senses.title: Legal instruments promising payment
senses.definition: legal documents such as promissory notes that bind a party to pay
senses.definitionCN: 本票等把一方约束在付款义务上的法律文书
senses.example: The merchant deposited the securities with his bank.
senses.exampleCN: 商人把那些付款凭证存进了银行。
senses.why: In commercial law a security can be a written promise to pay, so the same plural covers paper that creates a legal obligation.
senses.whyCN: 在商法中，证券也可以是一纸付款承诺，因此同一个复数形式也涵盖产生法律义务的文书。

senses.title: Assets pledged as collateral
senses.definition: assets deposited to guarantee a loan or obligation
senses.definitionCN: 为担保贷款或义务而交存的资产
senses.example: He pledged his securities against the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 他用自己的证券为这笔贷款作担保。
senses.why: Here the instrument is used as a shield: the lender holds the security so that a default can be covered by selling it.
senses.whyCN: 这里的工具被当作盾牌：出借人握有担保品，违约时便可出售以弥补损失。

senses.title: The securities industry
senses.definition: the sector of firms that issue, trade or advise on such instruments
senses.definitionCN: 发行、交易或为此类工具提供咨询的行业
senses.example: She spent twenty years working in securities.
senses.exampleCN: 她在证券行业工作了二十年。
senses.why: A mass of instruments and the firms handling them come to be named by the instruments themselves, so the plural stands for an entire trade.
senses.whyCN: 大量工具与处理这些工具的机构，最终以工具本身来命名，于是复数形式代表整个行业。

intro.en: Securities is the plural of security, a word built on Latin cura 'care' with the prefix se- 'without'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: securities 是 security 的复数；security 由拉丁语 cura「忧虑、照料」加前缀 se-「无」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cura meant care, concern or anxiety, and it built words about protecting against trouble.
items.cn: cura 意为照料、忧虑、担心，构成了一批表示防患于未然的词。

items.en: Securitas meant freedom from care or anxiety, a state in which nothing threatens.
items.cn: securitas 意为无忧无虑、免于焦虑，是一种没有威胁的状态。

items.en: Through French the word entered English as a state of safety or certainty, and later as a guarantee against loss.
items.cn: 经法语进入英语后，它先指安全或确定的状态，后来指防损失的保证。

items.en: Tradable claims on debt or ownership came to be called securities because a paper certificate gave the holder assurance of value.
items.cn: 可交易的债权或所有权凭证被称为 securities，因为一纸证书给了持有人关于价值的保障。

items.en: Company and securities law separated the traded instrument from the general idea of safety, fixing the plural as a technical term.
items.cn: 公司法与证券法把可交易工具与一般「安全」概念分开，使复数形式固定为专业术语。

note.en: The first group shares the same root or looks nearly identical; the second group lists other financial instruments and nearby categories.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一词根或拼写几乎相同；第二组列出其他金融工具与相邻类别。

entries.definition: The singular can mean safety, a guarantee, or one financial instrument; the plural usually means the instruments as a class.
entries.definitionCN: 单数可指安全、保证或一件金融工具；复数通常指作为一类的金融工具。

entries.definition: A guarantee or a person who guarantees another's obligation; it is about backing a promise, not about traded paper.
entries.definitionCN: 担保或为他人义务作保的人；它关乎为承诺作保，而非可交易凭证。

entries.definition: Safe, or to make safe; it keeps the original sense of freedom from danger and lacks the financial plural.
entries.definitionCN: 安全的，或使安全；保留「免于危险」的原义，没有金融上的复数用法。

entries.definition: The process of pooling assets and issuing tradable securities backed by them; it is the action, not the instruments.
entries.definitionCN: 把资产打包并发行以其为支撑的可交易证券的过程；它是动作，不是工具本身。

entries.definition: Shares, treated as a class; equities are one kind of security, not the whole class.
entries.definitionCN: 作为一类的股份；股票是证券的一种，而非全部。

entries.definition: Debt instruments issued by governments or companies; bonds are another kind of security.
entries.definitionCN: 政府或公司发行的债务工具；债券是证券的另一类。

entries.definition: A general finance term for contracts and documents with monetary value; securities is the narrower legal category.
entries.definitionCN: 金融中对具有货币价值的合约与文书的统称；证券是更窄的法律类别。

entries.definition: Anything bought to produce a return, including property and gold; securities are only the tradable paper part.
entries.definitionCN: 为产生回报而购买的任何东西，包括房产与黄金；证券只是其中可交易的那部分纸面资产。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin root for care, real fixed phrases and real related words.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语「忧虑」词根、真实固定搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: Security first meant freedom from care; a paper that removes worry about value became a security.
normal.cn: security 本义是免于忧虑；能消除价值担忧的一纸凭证便成了证券。

normal.en: The plural is the class word: stocks, bonds and notes are all securities.
normal.cn: 复数形式是类名词：股票、债券与票据都是证券。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the field: securities market, securities firm, securities law.
normal.cn: 固定搭配给这个领域分类：证券市场、证券公司、证券法。

normal.en: Securities can be debt or equity, which are two ways of holding a claim.
normal.cn: 证券可以是债务或权益，这是持有权利的两种方式。

normal.en: Pledged securities act as collateral, so the word returns to its old sense of guarantee.
normal.cn: 用作质押的证券充当担保品，这个词于是回到它古老的「保证」义。

abstract.en: Picture a wallet of stamped papers, each able to turn into money at a shout.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠盖印的纸，每一张都能在一声喊价中变成钱。

abstract.en: Picture the paper dissolving into a number on a screen, still carrying the same claim.
abstract.cn: 想象纸张消融成屏幕上的一串数字，却仍携带同样的权利。

abstract.en: Picture a promise and an ownership share drawn as two different keys to the same lock.
abstract.cn: 想象把承诺与所有权份额画成开同一把锁的两把不同钥匙。

examples.en: The firm was fined for misleading buyers of securities.
examples.cn: 该公司因误导证券买家而被罚款。

examples.en: Foreign investors may purchase government securities freely.
examples.cn: 外国投资者可以自由购买政府证券。

examples.en: She keeps a small part of her savings in securities.
examples.cn: 她把一小部分储蓄放在证券上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安心」的凭证——拿着它，价值有保障，还能在市场上卖掉 → 证券

root: security 出自拉丁语 securitas「无忧、安全」，由 se-「无」加 cura「忧虑、照料」构成；后指能带来价值保障的书面凭证，复数 securities 固定为证券。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses divide the class by what the paper represents: a tradable claim, a loan, an ownership share, a state-backed debt, a certificate, a promise to pay, a pledge and an entire industry.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按纸面所代表的东西来划分这一类：可交易权利、贷款、所有权份额、国家背书的债务、凭证、付款承诺、质押品与整个行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of stamped papers, each convertible into money at a shout.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠盖章的纸，每一张都能在喊价中换成钱。

branches.en: THE CLASS: the plural names tradable financial instruments as a whole.
branches.cn: 类别：复数形式统称可交易的金融工具。

branches.en: LENDING BRANCH: debt securities, including those issued by governments, represent money lent.
branches.cn: 借贷分支：债务证券，包括政府发行的债务证券，代表借出的资金。

branches.en: OWNERSHIP BRANCH: equity securities and share certificates represent a portion owned.
branches.cn: 所有权分支：权益证券与股份凭证代表所拥有的一部分。

branches.en: LEGAL PAPER: a promise to pay or an asset pledged as collateral turns the instrument into a safeguard.
branches.cn: 法律纸面：付款承诺或作为质押品的资产，把工具变成一种保障。

branches.en: TRADE AS A WHOLE: the instruments give their name to the industry that deals in them.
branches.cn: 整体行业：这些工具把名字给了经营它们的行业。

intro.en: Securities belongs to the Latin family of cura, and its derived words move between safety, guarantee and the packaging of assets.
intro.cn: securities 属于拉丁语 cura 一族，其派生词在安全、担保与资产打包之间移动。

latinIntro.en: Latin cura gives security, surety, assure and secure; the prefix se- adds the sense of being free from care.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cura 衍生出 security、surety、assure 与 secure；前缀 se- 增添「免于忧虑」的意思。

items.exampleCN: 这个词干带着免于忧虑的意思。

The guard provides security at night.

items.meaningCN: 把资产打包为证券的过程
items.example: Securitization spread risk across many buyers.
items.exampleCN: 证券化把风险分散给许多买家。

工作不稳定让员工担忧。

items.exampleCN: 他叔叔为这笔贷款作担保。

definition_zh: 出借人；放贷方；贷款机构；出借物品者；法律上的出借人
definition_en: a person or institution that gives money or goods to another on the understanding of repayment or return
core_image: 桌子一端的人把合同推过去，另一端的人接过钱，归还日期写在纸的中央
scene: 签约桌上，放款方把合同推到对面，逐条说明利率与还款期限。 The lender asked for two guarantors before signing.
sceneCN: 这里 lender 指「放贷方」（第 1 个义项：把钱借出、等待归还的人或机构）；句意为放贷方在签约前要求两名担保人。图中可辨识物件：合同、利率表、印章、担保人签名栏。

senses.title: A person who lends money
senses.definition: a person who gives money to another on the understanding that it will be repaid
senses.definitionCN: 把钱交给他人、并约定归还的人
senses.example: The lender asked for two guarantors before signing.
senses.exampleCN: 放贷方在签约前要求两名担保人。
senses.why: lend plus the agent ending -er names the giver in the transaction, the mirror image of the borrower.
senses.whyCN: lend 加施事后缀 -er，指交易中的给出方，与借款人正好相对。

senses.title: A financial institution in the business
senses.titleCN: 从事放贷业务的金融机构
senses.definition: a bank, building society or finance company whose business is to make loans
senses.definitionCN: 以发放贷款为业务的银行、建房互助会或金融公司
senses.example: Several lenders compete for the same mortgage.
senses.exampleCN: 几家放贷机构为同一笔按揭竞争。
senses.why: once lending became an industry, the agent noun came to name firms as well as individuals.
senses.whyCN: 当放贷成为一门行业，这个施事名词也用来指公司，而不只是个人。

senses.title: One who lends an object
senses.definition: a person who allows another to use an object temporarily and expects it back
senses.definitionCN: 允许他人临时使用某物、并期待归还的人
senses.example: The lender of the bicycle wants it back by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 借出自行车的人希望星期五前收回。
senses.why: the money sense is the dominant one, but the verb lends itself to any object handed over for temporary use.
senses.whyCN: 金钱义占主导，但这个动词也可用于任何临时交出的物件。

senses.title: The party who lends in law
senses.definition: in bailment for use, the party who gives property while keeping ownership and expecting its return
senses.definitionCN: 在使用借贷关系中交出财产、保留所有权并期待返还的一方
senses.example: As lender, she retained ownership of the tools.
senses.exampleCN: 作为出借人，她保留着工具的所有权。
senses.why: law separates the giver from the holder, and the giver is named with the ordinary agent noun.
senses.whyCN: 法律把交付方与持有人分开，交付方就用这个普通施事名词来指称。

senses.title: A sovereign or international lender
senses.definition: a state, fund or international body that lends to governments or large projects
senses.definitionCN: 向政府或大型项目放贷的国家、基金或国际机构
senses.example: Foreign lenders restructured the debt last year.
senses.exampleCN: 外国贷款方去年重组了这笔债务。
senses.why: states lend on the same terms as banks, so the word scales from a person to a treasury.
senses.whyCN: 国家按与银行相同的条件放贷，因此这个词可以从个人放大到国库。

senses.title: A supplier who extends credit
senses.definition: a seller who hands over goods before payment and so carries the risk of non-payment
senses.definitionCN: 在收款前先交货、因而承担不付款风险的卖方
senses.example: The supplier acted as lender while the goods were unpaid.
senses.exampleCN: 货款未付期间，供应商实际上充当了出借方。
senses.why: credit is a loan in kind, so a supplier who waits for payment is lending the value of the goods.
senses.whyCN: 赊账是实物形式的贷款，因此等待付款的供货方借出的是货物的价值。

senses.title: Any source that grants temporarily
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：暂时给予的来源
senses.definition: figuratively, a person or thing that supplies something for a time without giving it away
senses.definitionCN: 比喻上指临时提供某物、并不真正送出的来源
senses.example: Memory is a stern lender of borrowed scenes.
senses.exampleCN: 记忆是一个严厉的出借者，只借出场景而不送出。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the key condition: what is lent must eventually be given back.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了关键条件：借出之物终须归还。

senses.title: A historical moneylender
senses.definition: historically, a private person who lent coin at interest, often under legal caps
senses.definitionCN: 历史上以利息放贷的私人，常受法定上限约束
senses.example: The old lender charged interest that the law capped.
senses.exampleCN: 这位旧时放债者收取的利息受法律上限约束。
senses.why: before banks served ordinary people, private lenders filled the gap, and the word carries that history.
senses.whyCN: 在银行为普通人服务之前，私人放贷者填补了空缺，这个词带着那段历史。

intro.en: Lender is an English agent noun on lend, a native verb from Old English lænan. Nothing in it comes from Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: lender 是英语在 lend 之上构成的施事名词，而 lend 是来自古英语 lænan 的本族动词，其中没有拉丁成分。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lænan meant 'to lend, to grant the use of', and came from læn 'a loan', the same stock that produced the modern noun loan.
items.cn: lænan 意为「借出、准许使用」，来自 læn「借款」，与现代名词 loan 同出一源。

items.en: The verb belongs to a Germanic family that includes Dutch lenen and German leihen, all built on the idea of leaving something with another.
items.cn: 这个动词属日耳曼语族，包括荷兰语 lenen 与德语 leihen，都建立在「把某物留在他人处」这一概念上。

items.en: The ending -er is the native English agent suffix, so lender is simply the one who lends; the word is recorded from the twelfth century.
items.cn: 词尾 -er 是英语本族施事后缀，因此 lender 就是出借的人；该词自 12 世纪有记录。

items.en: As banking grew, lender widened from a private person to a firm, and phrases such as mortgage lender followed.
items.cn: 随着银行业发展，lender 从私人扩展到机构，mortgage lender 一类说法随之出现。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word scaled again, naming states and international funds that lend to governments.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪，这个词再次放大，用来指向政府放贷的国家与国际基金。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest record is not precisely dated, and the deeper pre-Germanic root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：最早记录没有确切年代，日耳曼语之前的更深词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same lending stem; group two holds the parties and instruments that sit on either side of a loan.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「借出」词干的形式；第二组是贷款两侧的人与工具。

entries.definition: The act of giving temporarily; lender is the person who performs it.
entries.definitionCN: 临时给出的动作；lender 是执行这一动作的人。

entries.definition: The sum or object lent; the lender gives the loan.
entries.definitionCN: 借出的款项或物件；放贷方给出这笔贷款。

entries.definition: The person who receives the loan; lender and borrower are defined against each other.
entries.definitionCN: 接受贷款的人；放贷方与借款人相互定义。

entries.definition: A central bank that lends when no other lender will; the phrase is a title, not a separate word.
entries.definitionCN: 在其他放贷方都不肯放贷时提供贷款的中央银行；这是固定称谓，不是另一个词。

entries.definition: A person to whom money is owed; a lender is a creditor while the loan is outstanding, but a creditor need not have lent cash.
entries.definitionCN: 被欠款的人；贷款未清时放贷方就是债权人，但债权人不一定借出过现金。

entries.definition: One who puts money in for a return from profits; a lender only expects repayment and interest.
entries.definitionCN: 投入资金以分享利润的人；放贷方只期待还款与利息。

entries.definition: A lender who takes an object as security and lends a fraction of its value.
entries.definitionCN: 以物品作担保、按其价值的一部分放贷的人。

entries.definition: A person who promises to repay if the borrower fails; not a lender, but the lender's protection.
entries.definitionCN: 承诺在借款人违约时偿还的人；不是放贷方，而是放贷方的保障。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: lend + -er: the person who lends; the ending is the ordinary English agent suffix.
normal.cn: lend 加 -er：出借的人；这个词尾就是英语普通的施事后缀。

normal.en: The family runs lend, lent, lending, lender, loan and borrower.
normal.cn: 同族包括 lend、lent、lending、lender、loan 与 borrower。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: a mortgage lender, a private lender, the lender of last resort.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：按揭放贷机构、私人放贷者、最后贷款人。

normal.en: Lender and borrower are mirror terms: one gives, one receives.
normal.cn: lender 与 borrower 是一对镜像词：一个给，一个受。

normal.en: Lender is not Latin; it is the native verb plus the native suffix.
normal.cn: lender 不是拉丁词；它是本族动词加本族词尾。

abstract.en: Picture a hand holding the other end of a string tied to a coin.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手握着绳子的另一端，绳头系着一枚硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a chair lent to a guest who is expected to leave it by the door.
abstract.cn: 想象一把借给客人的椅子，客人离开时须放回门边。

abstract.en: Picture a clock that lends minutes and always takes them back.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟借出分钟，又总会收回。

examples.en: The lender requires proof of income.
examples.cn: 放贷方要求提供收入证明。

examples.en: Small lenders were hit hardest by the rate rise.
examples.cn: 利率上升对小型放贷机构打击最大。

examples.en: The central bank acted as lender of last resort.
examples.cn: 中央银行充当了最后贷款人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「lend（借出）+ er（人）」——把东西借出去的人 → 出借人、放贷方

root: 古英语 lænan「借出」+ 本族施事后缀 -er；lænan 来自 læn「借款」，与古诺斯语 lán、现代 loan 同源。无拉丁来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one role: the person on the giving side of a temporary transfer, whether an individual, a bank, an object's owner, a state, a supplier or a metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个角色展开：临时转移中处于给出方的那个人，无论他是个人、银行、物主、国家、供货方，还是一个比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand lets go of a coin while the other end of the string stays with the giver.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手松开硬币，绳子的另一端仍留在给出者手里。

branches.en: THE PERSON: one who lends money and one who lends a bicycle are the same role.
branches.cn: 人：借钱给人的人与借出自行车的人是同一个角色。

branches.en: LENDING AS BUSINESS: a bank and a supplier waiting for payment both carry the risk.
branches.cn: 作为业务的出借：银行与等待付款的供货方都承担风险。

branches.en: THE LEGAL ROLE: ownership stays with the giver while use passes over.
branches.cn: 法律角色：使用权转出，所有权仍留在给出方。

branches.en: THE SOVEREIGN ROLE: the same terms writ large between states.
branches.cn: 国家角色：同样的条件在国与国之间放大。

branches.en: OUTSIDE FINANCE: a metaphor for any temporary giver, and the memory of private moneylenders.
branches.cn: 金融之外：既可比喻任何暂时给予者，也承载私人放债者的记忆。

intro.en: The word is one native verb plus one native agent ending, so its parts are English through and through.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个本族动词加一个本族施事词尾，两个部分都彻头彻尾属于英语。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here; Latin would express the lender with creditor or faenerator, words built on different roots.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁来源；拉丁语会用 creditor 或 faenerator 表达放贷者，那些词建立在不同的词根上。

items.example: The ending marks the doer of the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记动作的执行者。

items.example: She lent him the car for a day.
The loan fell due in May.
The fund keeps a lendable reserve.
items.exampleCN: 该基金保留一笔可出借的储备。

definition_zh: 恳求；哀求；苦苦哀求
definition_en: to ask someone earnestly and anxiously for something
core_image: 双膝跪地、双手合十仰起的哀求姿态
scene: 囚犯隔着铁栏抓住母亲的手。 The prisoner beseeched the judge for one more chance.
sceneCN: 这里 beseeched 是「恳求、哀求」（第 1 个义项：急切焦虑地请求）；句意是囚犯恳求法官再给一次机会。

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词转形容词，义为「哀求的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「哀求地」
基础词，义为「寻求」，beseech 与之同源相关

senses.title: To ask eagerly and anxiously
senses.definition: to beg someone earnestly, often with urgency or distress
senses.definitionCN: 急切而焦虑地向人恳求，常带迫切与痛苦
senses.example: The prisoner beseeched the judge for one more chance.
senses.exampleCN: 囚犯恳求法官再给一次机会。
senses.why: Be- strengthens seek, so it is seeking with all one's heart.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 be- 强化 seek（寻求），即全心全力地求。

senses.title: To entreat as in prayer or formal speech
senses.definition: to make an earnest appeal, as in prayers or old-fashioned letters
senses.definitionCN: 如祈祷或旧式书信中的郑重恳请
senses.example: I beseech you to hear my whole defence.
senses.exampleCN: 我恳请您听完我的全部申辩。
senses.why: The urgent seeking rises into solemn appeal.
senses.whyCN: 急切的「求」升格为庄重的「恳请」。

intro.en: Beseech is the prefix be- plus seek, an Old English verb of searching.
intro.cn: beseech 由前缀 be- 加 seek 构成，seek 是古英语表「寻找」的动词。

items.en: the root sag- meant to track down, to seek out.
items.cn: 词根 sag- 意为「追踪、寻出」（重构形式）。

items.en: secan meant to seek, to visit, to pursue.
items.cn: 古英语 secan 意为「寻找、拜访、追寻」。

items.en: beseken meant to seek earnestly, to entreat.
items.cn: 中古英语 beseken 意为「恳切寻求、恳求」。

items.en: beseech settled in the thirteenth century as a solemn begging word.
items.cn: 十三世纪 beseech 定型为庄重的恳求词。

items.en: it now sounds literary, with the irregular form besought alongside beseeched.
items.cn: 如今略显书面，不规则形式 besought 与 beseeched 并存。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the be- prefix or the seek root; the near-meaning group gathers begging words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 be- 前缀或 seek 词基；近义组汇集哀求类词。

entries.definition: to look for
entries.definitionCN: 寻求——beseech 的词基

entries.definition: to surround with armed forces
entries.definitionCN: 围攻——形近的 be- 动词，意义无关

entries.definition: the irregular past of beseech
entries.definitionCN: beseech 的不规则过去式

entries.definition: to beg urgently and tearfully
entries.definitionCN: 哀求；情感更激烈

entries.definition: to ask earnestly, literary
entries.definitionCN: 恳求；书面语色彩浓

entries.definition: to beg or argue earnestly
entries.definitionCN: 恳求；答辩；日常常用

normalIntro.cn: beseech 是 be- 加 seek：倾尽全力的寻求。

normal.en: The irregular past is besought.
normal.cn: 不规则过去式是 besought。

normal.en: Beseech implies urgency and distress.

normal.en: The adjective is beseeching.
normal.cn: 形容词是 beseeching。

normal.cn: implore 更激烈、更含泪。

abstract.en: See clasped hands raised toward a bench.
abstract.cn: 看朝审判席高高举起合十的双手。

abstract.en: Feel a tug on your sleeve that will not stop.
abstract.cn: 感受袖口不肯停的拉扯。

abstract.en: Picture eyes wide open like a pleading dog.
abstract.cn: 想象像哀恳的狗一样圆睁的双眼。

examples.en: The prisoner beseeched the judge for one more chance.
examples.cn: 囚犯恳求法官再给一次机会。

examples.en: I beseech you to hear my whole defence.
examples.cn: 我恳请您听完我的全部申辩。

examples.en: She gave him a beseeching look from the doorway.

senses.title: The activity of flying

intro.en: Aviation is a modern coinage from Latin avis, bird, with the ending -ation; it was formed in French in the 1860s for the idea of mechanical flight.
intro.cn: aviation 是近代由拉丁语 avis「鸟」加 -ation 词尾造出的词；1860 年代在法语中成形，用来指机械飞行这一构想。

items.en: A root meaning bird lies behind aviary and the Latin word avis.
items.cn: 一个表示「鸟」的词根支撑着 aviary 与拉丁语 avis。

items.en: Latin avis meant bird, the natural model for any thought of human flight.
items.cn: 拉丁语 avis 意为「鸟」，是人类飞行构想的天然范本。

items.en: Aviarium named a place where birds were kept, giving English aviary.
items.cn: aviarium 指养鸟之处，产生英语 aviary。

items.en: A French writer coined aviation in 1863 from avis plus -ation for aerial navigation.
items.cn: 一位法国作者于 1863 年由 avis 加 -ation 造出 aviation，指空中航行。

items.en: English took the word within three years, while powered flight was still decades away.
items.cn: 英语在三年内就借入该词，而动力飞行还要等上几十年。

items.en: After 1903 the word grew into the name of a whole industry and its regulation.
items.cn: 1903 年之后，这个词扩展为整个产业及其监管的名称。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the avi family; the near-meaning group lists other names for flight as a science or a trade.
note.cn: 形近组保留 avi 词族；近义组列出把飞行当作科学或行业的其他名称。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the bird craft: the whole trade of building and running aircraft, and the flying itself sorted by purpose.

branches.en: A trade employing millions.

definition_zh: 事后想起的想法；事后的补充
definition_en: an idea or addition that occurs to someone only after the main action or statement is finished
core_image: 关门后拍额头：事情办完才想起漏了的话
scene: 邮件发出去两分钟后，她才想起忘了问时间。 She asked about the venue first and mentioned the dress code as an afterthought.
sceneCN: 这里 afterthought 是「事后的补充」（第 1 个义项：主事完成后才想起补上的想法）；句意是她先问了地点，末了才顺口补了句着装要求。

pos.zh: 事后想起的想法；事后补充

collocations.zh: 安全被当作事后才考虑的事

senses.title: An idea occurring after the event
senses.titleCN: 事后想起的想法；事后补充
senses.definition: a remark or item added when the main part is already done, showing it was not planned in advance
senses.definitionCN: 主要部分完成之后才补上的一句话或一项内容，说明事先并未计划
senses.example: She asked about the venue first and mentioned the dress code as an afterthought.
senses.exampleCN: 她先问了地点，末了才顺口补了句着装要求。
senses.why: The compound is literal: a thought that arrives after. Its core image is the missed item remembered too late.
senses.whyCN: 复合词结构即字面义：「之后」才到来的「想法」；核心画面是事过之后才想起的遗漏。

senses.title: Something given too little and too late
senses.titleCN: 不被重视的次要事物；临时敷衍的添加
senses.definition: something added carelessly at the end and treated as unimportant
senses.definitionCN: 末尾随手加上、被当作无关紧要的东西
senses.example: Accessibility was an afterthought in the design, bolted on at the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 无障碍设计在这套方案里只是事后补丁，最后一刻才草草加上。
senses.why: Because an afterthought was never planned, it is by definition second-class; the word turned that defect into a criticism.
senses.whyCN: 既然是「事后才想起」，就注定不是重点；词义由此转出批评色彩——「敷衍的、次要的添加」。

intro.en: A transparent English compound of after plus thought, modelled on earlier after-words.
intro.cn: 一目了然的英语复合词：after（之后）+ thought（想法），仿照更早的 after- 系词构成。

items.en: The root *terk- (to twist, to form) is generally linked to think and thought.
items.cn: 一般认为 think / thought 与重构词根 *terk-（搓转、成形）相关。

items.en: after and þoht existed separately; compounds with after- named whatever followed.
items.cn: 古英语中 after 与 þoht 各自独立；after- 系复合词命名「随后出现的事物」。

items.en: afterthought appears in the sense of later reflection, sometimes regret.
items.cn: 中古英语出现 afterthought，意为「事后的思索」，有时带悔意。

items.en: The sense settled on an addition made afterwards, often contrasted with forethought.
items.cn: 十七至十八世纪词义固定为「事后添加」，常与 forethought（预先考虑）相对。

items.en: The phrase as an afterthought is idiomatic; the word often criticises neglected priorities.
items.cn: 现代英语中 as an afterthought 已成语化；该词常用于批评被忽视的优先事项。

note.en: Afterthought is the mirror of forethought; it differs from a simple addition by arriving late and unplanned.
note.cn: afterthought 与 forethought 互为镜像；它与普通的「补充」不同，在于来得晚且不在计划内。

entries.definition: planning or care for the future in advance

entries.definition: a delayed result of an action
entries.definitionCN: 后效；后遗症——同为 after- 复合词

normalIntro.en: Read the compound literally: a thought that comes after.
normalIntro.cn: 按字面拆读：after（之后）+ thought（想法）＝ 之后才来的想法。

normal.en: after + thought: the idea arrived too late
normal.cn: after + thought：想法来得太迟

normal.en: as an afterthought is the fixed phrase: tacked on at the end
normal.cn: as an afterthought 是固定搭配：末尾随手补上一句

normal.en: afterthought versus forethought: too late versus just in time
normal.cn: afterthought（事后才想）对照 forethought（提前想到）

normal.en: safety as an afterthought: criticism of neglected priorities
normal.cn: safety as an afterthought 批评「安全成了事后才考虑的事」

examples.en: The greenhouse looked like an afterthought, squeezed between garage and fence.
examples.cn: 那间温室像是事后加盖的，挤在车库和栅栏之间。

examples.en: He apologized for forgetting her birthday, calling it a terrible lapse rather than an afterthought.
examples.cn: 他为忘记她的生日道歉，说这是严重疏忽，并非事后才想起。

examples.en: User privacy should never be an afterthought in app design.
examples.cn: 在应用设计中，用户隐私绝不应是事后才想起的补丁。

sensesIntro.en: From a thought arriving late grows both the neutral sense of an added remark and the critical sense of something neglected.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「迟到的念头」长出中性的「事后补充」，再长出带批评色彩的「临时敷衍、不被重视的添加」。

items.en: Junctio meant a joining or a joint.

items.en: Old French jonction carried the sense of a joining.

items.en: Junction entered English for a place where things meet.

items.en: Dis- gave disjunction, a state of being unjoined.

examples.cn: 日期上的一处断裂削弱了这个论点。

dict_mnemonic.text: disjunction ＝ dis-（分开）＋ junction（连接处，拉丁语 junctio，来自 jungere「连接」，与 join、joint、conjunction 同根）＝连接被打开，「分离、析取」。

root: 拉丁语 jungere（连接）→ junctio（接合）→ 古法语 jonction → 英语 junction → 加 dis- 成 disjunction

sensesIntro.en: A link opened: carriages uncoupled, a circuit cut in two and a timeline with a missing stretch.
sensesIntro.cn: 被打开的连接：脱钩的车厢、剪成两段的电路与缺了一段的时间线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rail carriages with the coupling opened between them while a cut circuit lights two separate lamps
core.cn: 核心意象：两节车厢之间的挂钩被打开，同时一条剪断的电路点亮两盏各自的灯

branches.en: Theory and practice uncoupled like carriages.
branches.cn: 像车厢一样脱钩的理论与实务。

branches.en: A cut circuit where either lamp can light.
branches.cn: 任一盏灯都能亮的剪断电路。

branches.en: A timeline with a missing stretch.
branches.cn: 缺了一段的时间线。

branches.en: Both show parts that no longer depend on each other.
branches.cn: 两者都显示不再相互依赖的部分。

branches.en: Both leave a gap you can point at.
branches.cn: 两者都留下一个指得出来的缺口。

intro.en: Disjunction is dis- plus junction; the join root also builds join, joint, conjunction and juncture.
intro.cn: disjunction 由 dis- 加 junction 构成；连接这个词根也造出 join、joint、conjunction 与 juncture。

latinIntro.en: Latin jungere means to join, junctio a joining and nectere to bind.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 jungere 意为连接，junctio 意为接合，nectere 意为绑。

definition_zh: 暂定的；试探性的；初步的；迟疑不决的
definition_en: not yet final and open to change, or done cautiously as a first test
core_image: 谈判桌上摆着一份还没定稿的备忘录，签字旁边留着一行小字：待双方董事会批准
scene: 谈判结束时，双方在一份仍可修改的备忘录上签了名，各自都留了一步退路。 They reached a tentative agreement that still needed approval from both boards.
sceneCN: 这里指尚未最终确定、仍可更改（第 1 个义项：暂定的）；句意为双方达成了一份仍待两家董事会批准的初步协议。图中可辨识物件：备忘录、签名栏、一行待批准的小字、会议桌。

pos.zh: 暂定的；试探性的；初步的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「试探性地；暂定地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「试探性；迟疑」
由同一拉丁动词经法语构成，义为「尝试」，属同源而非直接派生
由同一拉丁动词的另一形态经法语构成，义为「引诱；试探」，属同源而非直接派生

senses.title: Not final
senses.definition: agreed or set for now but still open to change
senses.definitionCN: 暂时确定、但仍可更改的
senses.example: The schedule is tentative and will be confirmed on Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 日程是暂定的，周五才会确认。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to try, and what is tried is not yet settled.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「尝试」，试过的东西自然还没有定下来。

senses.title: An initial agreement
senses.definition: an arrangement accepted in outline, pending formal approval
senses.definitionCN: 在要点上接受、等待正式批准的安排
senses.example: The two sides signed a tentative agreement and left the details to their lawyers.
senses.exampleCN: 双方签了一份初步协议，细节留给各自的律师。
senses.why: An agreement is tentative while the signatures still wait for approval upstairs.
senses.whyCN: 协议在签名还等着上级批准时，就是初步的。

senses.title: A testing first step
senses.definition: a cautious action taken to see how others react
senses.definitionCN: 为看看对方反应而谨慎采取的行动
senses.example: She took a tentative step into the new market before committing a full budget.
senses.exampleCN: 她先在新市场试探性地迈出一步，之后才投入全部预算。
senses.why: A step that tests the ground keeps the meaning of trying in the body.
senses.whyCN: 试探地面的一步，把「尝试」的含义落到了步子上。

senses.title: A cautious smile
senses.definition: a slight smile that asks whether it is welcome
senses.definitionCN: 轻微地笑一下，试探对方是否接受
senses.example: The new student gave a tentative smile and waited for an answer.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的学生试探性地笑了笑，等着对方回应。
senses.why: Here the uncertainty is social rather than factual, but the same caution shows.
senses.whyCN: 这里的不确定是社会性的而非事实性的，但同样的谨慎仍然可见。

senses.title: A provisional conclusion
senses.definition: a conclusion offered while evidence is still incomplete
senses.definitionCN: 在证据仍不完整时给出的结论
senses.example: Our tentative conclusion is that the effect is small, though more trials are needed.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的初步结论是效应不大，但仍需更多试验。
senses.why: A conclusion offered while data are still arriving is held provisionally by design.
senses.whyCN: 在数据仍陆续到来时给出的结论，按设计就是暂且持有的。

senses.title: A date that may move
senses.definition: a fixed date that everyone knows may be changed
senses.definitionCN: 大家都明白可能会改的已定日期
senses.example: We have a tentative date in June, subject to the permit.
senses.exampleCN: 我们暂定六月，还要看许可证。
senses.why: Setting a date provisionally is a way of planning without promising.
senses.whyCN: 把日期暂定下来，是一种「做计划但不作承诺」的办法。

senses.title: A hesitant tone
senses.definition: speaking in a way that shows one is unsure of the welcome
senses.definitionCN: 说话时显出不确定对方是否欢迎的样子
senses.example: He answered in a tentative voice, as if expecting to be corrected.
senses.exampleCN: 他迟疑地回答，好像随时准备被纠正。
senses.why: Caution moves from the plan to the voice, and the word now describes how someone speaks.
senses.whyCN: 谨慎从计划移到声音上，词于是描述一个人怎么说话。

senses.title: Exploratory in method
senses.definition: trying a small move in an unfamiliar situation before going further
senses.definitionCN: 在陌生情境里先小幅行动、再决定是否继续
senses.example: The first meetings were tentative, designed to test whether the teams could work together.
senses.exampleCN: 最初的几次会面是试探性的，用来检验两队是否能合作。
senses.why: A method is tentative when its first purpose is to find out whether it works at all.
senses.whyCN: 当一种方法的首要目的是弄清它究竟行不行，它就是试探性的。

intro.en: Tentative comes from Latin tentativus, trying or testing, from tentare, to try, a frequentative form of tendere, to stretch. English took it in the sixteenth century for statements and steps held only provisionally, and the idea of a trial has stayed at its centre.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 tentativus「尝试的、试探的」，出自动词 tentare「试」，而 tentare 是 tendere「伸展」的反复形式。十六世纪进入英语，用来指只是暂时拿出的说法与步骤，「试一试」的意思始终在核心。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch or aim, and its repeated form described trying something again and again.
items.cn: 这个词意为「伸展、指向」，其反复形式表示一次又一次地试。

items.en: Tentare meant to try, to test, and also to attack or probe.
items.cn: 这个词意为「试、试探」，也有「进攻、探察」之意。

items.en: The adjective described what was done by way of trial rather than as a settled act.
items.cn: 该形容词形容出于尝试而非定论所做的。

items.en: French used the adjective for experiments and provisional arrangements.
items.cn: 法语用它指实验与暂定的安排。

items.en: English applied it to opinions, plans and the first movements of a cautious person.
items.cn: 英语把它用于意见、计划以及谨慎者的最初动作。

items.en: Negotiation gave the word its common phrase, tentative agreement; the phrase's first recorded year is uncertain.
items.cn: 谈判给出它最常见的搭配「初步协议」；该搭配首见的年份不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the trying root or looks close; the second group names other kinds of provisional things. The note also separates tentative from tenable, which looks similar but comes from a different verb.
note.cn: 第一组共享「尝试」词根或形近；第二组指其他「暂时性」的说法。这里也把「暂定的」与形近但异源的「站得住脚的」分开。

entries.definition: In a cautious or provisional way.
entries.definitionCN: 指以试探或暂定的方式。

entries.definition: The quality of being provisional or hesitant.
entries.definitionCN: 指暂定或迟疑的性质。

entries.definition: To try to do something; the same Latin verb reached English through French.
entries.definitionCN: 指尝试做某事；同一拉丁动词经法语进入英语。

entries.definition: To lure or test someone; a different form of the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指引诱或试探某人；同一拉丁动词的另一形式。

entries.definition: Able to be defended; it comes from the verb meaning to hold, not to try.
entries.definitionCN: 指站得住脚、可辩护的；出自表示「握住」的动词，与「尝试」无关。

entries.definition: A principle held as true; from the same holding verb as tenable.
entries.definitionCN: 指被奉为真的原则；与「站得住脚」同出「握住」动词。

entries.definition: Arranged for present needs and expected to be replaced.
entries.definitionCN: 指为当前需要而设、预期会被替换的。

entries.definition: Coming before the main event as preparation.
entries.definitionCN: 指在正式活动之前、作为准备的。

entries.definition: Serving only for the time between two settled states.
entries.definitionCN: 指只在两个稳定状态之间暂时顶替的。

entries.definition: Done in order to find out rather than to settle.
entries.definitionCN: 指为了了解情况而非下定论所做的。

entries.definition: Slow to act because of uncertainty; it describes the person rather than the arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 指因不确定而行动迟缓，描述的是人而不是安排。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the unsigned contract, the first small step, the careful smile and the June date pencilled in.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用未定稿的备忘录、试探的一小步、谨慎的微笑与用铅笔写下的六月。

normal.en: A tentative deal is written in pencil, not in ink.
normal.cn: 初步协议用铅笔写，不用墨水。

normal.en: A tentative step is a foot testing the ice before the body follows.
normal.cn: 试探性的一步，是脚先试试冰面，身体再跟上。

normal.en: A tentative smile asks a question without words.
normal.cn: 试探性的微笑，是在不用言语地问一句。

normal.en: If the date is tentative, the invitation says so and nobody is blamed.
normal.cn: 日期若为暂定，请柬上会写明，事后也没人该被责怪。

normal.en: Tentative and tenable look alike, but one means tried and the other means holdable.
normal.cn: 「暂定的」与「站得住脚的」形近，一个意为「试过」，一个意为「握得住」。

abstract.en: Provisional things are honest about their own fragility, which is why they are trusted for a while.
abstract.cn: 暂定之物坦白自己的脆弱，所以反而能被信任一阵。

abstract.en: Every firm decision began as a tentative one that someone dared to repeat.
abstract.cn: 每个确定的决定，起初都是一个有人敢重复的暂定决定。

abstract.en: To try is to leave a door open; to settle is to close it, and both have their season.
abstract.cn: 尝试是留一扇门，确定是把门关上，两者各有其时。

examples.en: The committee adopted a tentative plan and asked for cost estimates.
examples.cn: 委员会采纳了一项暂定计划，并要求提供成本估算。

examples.en: He gave a tentative nod, then asked to see the contract again.
examples.cn: 他试探性地点了点头，随后要求再看一遍合同。

examples.en: The tentative date is 12 June, subject to the venue.
examples.cn: 暂定日期是六月十二日，还要看场地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「坦特提夫」：先「试」一下再说话，语气留半分，结论也留半分

root: 源于拉丁语中表示「伸展、指向」的动词，其反复形式义为「试、试探」，再加形容词尾，经法语进入英语。表示「尝试」「引诱」的英语词与之同源，但不是由它直接派生。十六世纪进入英语；「初步协议」这一搭配首见年份不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one caution: a provisional arrangement, an initial deal, a testing step, a cautious smile, a provisional conclusion, a movable date, a hesitant voice, and an exploratory method.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一种谨慎：暂定安排、初步协议、试探的一步、谨慎的微笑、初步结论、可改的日期、迟疑的语气与试探性的做法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signature goes on a memorandum that still carries a line asking for later approval.
core.cn: 核心意象：名字签在一份备忘录上，旁边还留着一行「待批准」。

branches.en: THE OPEN ARRANGEMENT: a plan or date that everyone knows may move.
branches.cn: 敞开的安排：人人都知道可能会变的计划或日期。

branches.en: THE FIRST VERSION: an initial deal or conclusion, subject to approval.
branches.cn: 最初版本：初步协议或结论，仍待批准。

branches.en: THE FIRST PROBE: a small action taken to read another person's reaction.
branches.cn: 探路的一步：先做一个动作，看看对方如何反应。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL HESITATION: a careful smile and a careful voice.
branches.cn: 社交上的迟疑：谨慎的微笑与谨慎的语气。

branches.en: EXPLORATORY BY METHOD: start small in an unfamiliar setting, then decide whether to continue.
branches.cn: 方法上的试探：在陌生情境里先做小步，再决定是否继续。

intro.en: Tentative is a Latin trying verb with two endings; its family covers trying, testing and the caution that goes with both.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「试」动词加词尾；词族覆盖尝试、试探以及随之而来的谨慎。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere, tentare and tentativus trace the path from stretching to trying to provisional.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「伸展」「试」「尝试的」三词，勾出从拉伸到尝试再到暂定的路径。

items.example: The deeper root of the family.
The repeated form that carries the trying sense.
items.exampleCN: 承载「尝试」义的反复形式。
它给出这个英语形容词。

items.example: It marks the word as describing a manner.
items.exampleCN: 它标明该词描述一种方式。

items.example: A same-root word, not a derivative of tentative.
items.exampleCN: 同源词，不是由本词派生。
另一个经法语而来的同源词。

由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「试探性」
