definition_zh: 部署；调配；展开；投入使用
definition_en: the act of moving people, equipment or software into position and putting them into use
core_image: 一队士兵从行军队形展开，铺满整条防线
scene: 这里指「部署」。 The deployment of rescue teams began within an hour of the earthquake.
sceneCN: 这里 deployment 是「部署、调配」（第 2 个义项：把应急力量派到位置并投入使用）；句意：地震后一小时内，救援队的部署就开始了。图中可辨识物件：救援车、帐篷、担架、地图上标出的集结点。

pos.zh: 部署；调配；展开；投入使用

senses.title: Moving troops into position
senses.titleCN: 军事部署：把部队摆到该在的位置
senses.definition: the movement of military forces into the positions where they will operate
senses.definitionCN: 把军事力量调动到其将执行任务的位置
senses.example: The deployment of two brigades to the border took three days.
senses.exampleCN: 两个旅部署到边境花了三天。
senses.why: deploy comes from 'to unfold'. Troops folded into columns are unfolded across a front, so deployment is literally the spreading out of a force.
senses.whyCN: deploy 本义是“展开”。折成纵队的部队被展开到整条正面，因此 deployment 字面上就是兵力的铺开。

senses.title: Sending emergency teams
senses.titleCN: 应急力量部署：把人派到现场
senses.definition: the dispatch of police, medical or rescue units to an incident
senses.definitionCN: 把警察、医疗或救援单位派往事件现场
senses.example: Rapid deployment of medical staff saved several injured passengers.
senses.exampleCN: 医护人员的快速部署救下了几名受伤乘客。
senses.why: The same unfolding happens on a smaller scale: folded units are spread across a site. The word does not require an army, only a force that must occupy ground.
senses.whyCN: 同样的展开发生在更小的尺度：成建制的单位被铺到一个现场。这个词不要求军队，只要求一支必须占据地面的力量。

senses.title: Allocating people and equipment
senses.titleCN: 资源调配：把人和设备放到需要处
senses.definition: the organized assignment of staff, money or equipment to tasks
senses.definitionCN: 把人员、资金或设备有组织地分配到任务上
senses.example: The deployment of engineers to the northern site slowed the southern work.
senses.exampleCN: 把工程师调往北部工地拖慢了南部的进度。
senses.why: Deployment implies a map: resources are folded up in one place and unfolded where needed. Allocation is the civilian version of the same operation.
senses.whyCN: deployment 隐含着地图：资源在一处被收拢，在需要处被展开。分配就是同一操作的民用版。

senses.title: Releasing software into service
senses.titleCN: 软件部署：把程序装到每台机器
senses.definition: the process of installing, configuring and activating software across systems
senses.definitionCN: 在各系统上安装、配置并启用软件的过程
senses.example: The deployment of the new scheduling system caused a day of confusion.
senses.exampleCN: 新排班系统的部署造成了一天的混乱。
senses.why: Code stored in a repository is folded away; deployment unfolds it onto many machines. The metaphor fits because the software is spread out where it will run.
senses.whyCN: 仓库里的代码是折起来收着的；部署把它展开到许多机器上。这个隐喻贴切，因为软件被铺到它要运行的地方。

senses.title: Putting arguments into play
senses.titleCN: 话术的运用：把论点摆上桌
senses.definition: the strategic use of words, skills or arguments to achieve an effect
senses.definitionCN: 为达到某种效果而策略性地使用言辞、技能或论点
senses.example: The report criticized the deployment of fear rather than evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 报告批评了用恐惧而不是证据来做说服。
senses.why: Rhetorical deployment treats arguments as troops: they are placed where they can do the most work. The military image is borrowed deliberately.
senses.whyCN: 修辞上的 deployment 把论点当成部队：把它们摆到最能发挥作用的位置。这里有意借用了军事意象。

senses.title: Unfolding something physically
senses.titleCN: 展开：把折起的东西铺开
senses.definition: the act of opening out or extending something that was folded
senses.definitionCN: 把折叠之物打开或伸展的动作
senses.example: The deployment of the solar wings took several minutes after launch.
senses.exampleCN: 发射后，太阳能翼的展开花了几分钟。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most literal sense. Modern French déployer still means 'to unfold', and English keeps that physical meaning in space and engineering writing.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老、最字面的义项。现代法语 déployer 仍表示“展开”，英语在航天与工程写作中保留了这一物理义。

senses.title: A fleet's operational tour
senses.titleCN: 舰队部署：一整轮海外执勤
senses.definition: the period during which a naval force operates away from its home base
senses.definitionCN: 海军力量离开母港在外执行任务的那段时间
senses.example: The carrier returned home after a seven-month deployment.
senses.exampleCN: 航母在为期七个月的部署后返回母港。
senses.why: A fleet spread across foreign waters is a deployed force. The noun shifts from the act of moving to the whole period of being spread out.
senses.whyCN: 散布在海外海域的舰队就是被部署的力量。这个名词从“调动的动作”转指“被铺开的整个时期”。

senses.title: Putting capital to work
senses.titleCN: 资金投放：把钱铺到项目上
senses.definition: the investment of funds or assets into projects expected to produce returns
senses.definitionCN: 把资金或资产投入预期产生回报的项目
senses.example: The fund's deployment into green energy reached two billion dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金投入绿色能源的资金达到二十亿美元。
senses.why: Capital held in reserve is folded up; once invested it is spread across projects. Finance borrowed the military word because both involve placing assets where they can act.
senses.whyCN: 留存的资本是折起来的；一旦投资就被铺到各个项目。金融借用这个军事词，因为两者都涉及把资产放到能发挥作用的位置。

intro.en: Deployment is the noun of deploy, borrowed from French déployer 'to unfold'. French traces it to Latin displicare, dis- 'apart' plus plicare 'to fold'. The military sense dominates English usage, and the software sense is recent.
intro.cn: deployment 是 deploy 的名词，借自法语 déployer“展开”。法语可追到拉丁 displicare，由 dis-“分开”和 plicare“折叠”构成。军事义主导了英语用法，软件义则是晚近才出现的。

items.en: plicare meant 'to fold, bend, twist'. A folded thing occupies less ground, so unfolding it is the act of spreading it across space.
items.cn: plicare 意为“折叠、弯、扭”。折起的东西占的地方小，把它打开就是让它铺满空间。

items.en: displicare adds dis- 'apart' to plicare, giving 'to unfold, spread out'. This Latin verb is also the ancestor of English display, a close doublet of deploy.
items.cn: displicare 给 plicare 加 dis-“分开”，意为“展开、铺开”。这个拉丁动词也是英语 display 的祖先，display 与 deploy 是一对近双式词。

items.en: Old French desplier became modern déployer, still the ordinary verb for unfolding a map or a sail. English borrowed the military form deploy in the 15th to 17th century; exact dating is uncertain.
items.cn: 古法语 desplier 演变为现代 déployer，至今仍是“展开地图或帆”的常用动词。英语在 15 至 17 世纪借入军事形式的 deploy，确切年代存疑。

items.en: By the 17th century deploy was a technical term for extending a body of troops from column into line. Deployment names that manoeuvre and, by extension, any placing of forces.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，deploy 已是把部队从纵队展开成横队的技术术语。deployment 命名这一机动，并引申指任何力量布置。

items.en: In the 20th century the word spread to police, rescue, equipment and resources. The common thread is still movement into position followed by use.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词扩展到警察、救援、设备和资源。共同线索仍是“进入位置后再投入使用”。

items.en: Software deployment appears in the late 20th century. Code is stored folded in a repository and unfolded onto servers, so the old metaphor survived the change of material.
items.cn: 软件部署出现于 20 世纪后期。代码折叠存放在仓库里，再展开到服务器上，因此旧隐喻在材料改变后依然存活。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the plicare root through different prefixes; the near-meaning group shares the idea of placing something where it can work.
note.cn: 形近组经不同前缀共享 plicare 词根；近义组都含“把某物放到能发挥作用之处”的意思。

entries.definition: to move forces or resources into position; to unfold. Deployment is the noun of this action.
entries.definitionCN: 把力量或资源调到位；展开。deployment 是这一动作的名词。

entries.definition: to deploy again or move to a new position. re- 'again' marks a second unfolding.
entries.definitionCN: 重新部署或调往新位置。re-“再次”标记第二次展开。

entries.tag: doublet from the same latin verb
entries.definition: to arrange something so it can be seen. It comes from the same displicare but stresses visibility rather than operational placement.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物摆出来给人看。它来自同一个 displicare，但强调可见性，而非作战位置。

entries.definition: the act of putting something in a particular place; it is neutral about whether the thing is then used.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物放到特定位置；它对之后是否投入使用不加说明。

entries.definition: the act of preparing and assembling forces for action; it stresses readiness rather than final placement.
entries.definitionCN: 为行动准备并集结力量；它强调准备就绪，而非最终位置。

entries.definition: the act of fixing equipment or software in place so it can work; common for software, but narrower than deployment.
entries.definitionCN: 把设备或软件装到位使其可运行；软件语境常用，但比 deployment 窄。

entries.definition: the assignment of resources to users or tasks; it concerns shares, while deployment concerns placement and use.
entries.definitionCN: 把资源分配给使用者或任务；它关注份额，而 deployment 关注位置与使用。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'apart' + plicare 'fold': to deploy is to unfold a force across the ground.
normal.cn: de-“分开”+ plicare“折叠”：deploy 就是把力量在地面上展开。

normal.en: display is a doublet: same Latin verb, but display is about being seen, deploy about being placed.
normal.cn: display 是同源双式词：同一个拉丁动词，但 display 讲被看见，deploy 讲被放置。

normal.en: The standard pairing is troop deployment; if you can say 'troops', you are in the military sense.
normal.cn: 标准搭配是 troop deployment；如果能接 troops，你就在军事义里。

normal.en: Software deployment keeps the same logic: code folded in a repository is unfolded onto servers.
normal.cn: 软件部署保持同一逻辑：仓库里折起的代码被展开到服务器上。

normal.en: redeployment is the same map drawn twice: units are folded up and unfolded somewhere else.
normal.cn: redeployment 是同一张地图画两次：单位被收拢，再在别处展开。

abstract.en: Think of a paper map folded into a pocket and then opened across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图折起来塞进口袋，再在桌面上整幅展开。

abstract.en: Think of a fan closed in a hand and then spread until every rib shows.
abstract.cn: 想象一把扇子收在手里，再展开到每根扇骨都露出。

abstract.en: Think of chess pieces lifted from a box and placed on every relevant square before play begins.
abstract.cn: 想象棋子在开局前从盒子里取出，摆到每一个相关格子。

examples.en: The deployment of additional nurses reduced waiting times in the emergency room.
examples.cn: 增派护士的部署缩短了急诊室的等候时间。

examples.en: The company delayed the deployment of the update until the weekend.
examples.cn: 公司把更新的部署推迟到周末。

examples.en: Critics questioned the deployment of public money into a risky venture.
examples.cn: 批评者质疑把公共资金投入高风险项目的做法。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地铺罗伊”——地上（de）铺（ploy）开洛伊的部队，一排排站好 → deployment 部署、展开

root: 法语 déployer“展开” ← 古法语 desplier ← 拉丁 displicare“展开”（dis-“分开”+ plicare“折叠”）；deploy + -ment 名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one motion: something folded or held in reserve is opened out and placed where it can act.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个动作：收着或折着的东西被打开，放到能发挥作用的位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: troops unfolding from column into a line across the front.
core.cn: 核心意象：部队从纵队展开成横贯正面的横队。

branches.en: THE TOUR: a fleet’s time abroad is the same deployment seen across a span of time.
branches.cn: 舰队部署：一整轮海外执勤，是同一部署在时间跨度上的看法。

branches.en: CIVILIAN FORCES AND RESOURCES: rescue teams and engineers are deployed exactly as troops are, by placing them where the need is.
branches.cn: 民用力量与资源：救援队与工程师的部署方式与部队相同，都是放到需要之处。

branches.en: SOFTWARE AND PHYSICAL UNFOLDING: code spread onto servers and a solar wing opening in orbit both repeat the literal unfolding.
branches.cn: 软件与物理展开：代码铺到服务器、太阳能翼在轨道打开，都重复了字面意义上的展开。

branches.en: ARGUMENTS AND CAPITAL: rhetoric and money are placed like forces, each deployed where it can produce the greatest effect.
branches.cn: 论点与资本：话术和金钱都像力量一样被放置，各自部署到最能产生效果的地方。

branches.en: THE BASE IMAGE: all extensions keep the idea of an organised body moving from storage into operational space.
branches.cn: 基础意象：所有引申都保留“有组织的整体从储备状态进入运作空间”的观念。

intro.en: Deployment is deploy plus -ment, a noun suffix of action or result. The Latin prefix and root are fused inside deploy; English productively adds re- and -able around it.
intro.cn: deployment 是 deploy 加 -ment（表动作或结果的名词后缀）。拉丁前缀与词根已融合在 deploy 内部；英语在它外面能产地加 re- 和 -able。

latinIntro.en: Latin plicare 'to fold' yields displicare 'unfold', explicare 'unfold, explain', implicare 'fold in', and replicare 'fold back'. English receives branches through French: deploy, display, exploit, employ.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 plicare“折叠”派生 displicare“展开”、explicare“展开、解释”、implicare“折进去”、replicare“折回”。英语经法语接收了各分支：deploy、display、exploit、employ。

items.meaning: to unfold; to move into position
items.meaningCN: 展开；部署（dis-“分开”+ plicare“折叠”）
items.example: The unit was deployed along the eastern ridge.
items.exampleCN: 该部队被部署在东侧山脊沿线。

items.meaning: the act or result of deploying
items.meaningCN: 部署；展开（-ment 构成动作或结果名词）
items.example: The deployment of the field hospital took a full day.
items.exampleCN: 野战医院的部署花了一整天。

items.meaningCN: 重新部署；调往别处（re-“再次”+ deploy）
items.example: Half the staff were redeployed to the new branch.
items.exampleCN: 一半员工被重新部署到新分公司。

items.example: Redeployment of the team followed the plant closure.
items.exampleCN: 工厂关闭后团队被重新部署。

items.meaningCN: 可部署的；可展开的（-able“能够被……”）
items.example: The reserve unit is deployable within twelve hours.
items.exampleCN: 预备役部队可在十二小时内完成部署。

items.meaningCN: 展示；陈列（同源双式词，强调被看见）
items.example: The samples were displayed on a long table.
items.exampleCN: 样品陈列在一张长桌上。

items.meaning: to unfold; to make full use of
items.meaningCN: 开发；利用（ex-“向外”+ plicare“折叠”，把潜力展开）
items.example: The company exploited a gap in the market.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司利用了一个市场空白。

items.meaning: to fold in; to use or hire
items.meaningCN: 雇用；使用（由“折进去、纳入其中”引申）
items.exampleCN: 这家实验室雇用了四十名研究员。

definition_zh: 精算师；保险精算师
definition_en: a person whose job is to calculate insurance risks and premiums using statistics
core_image: 一堆保单和表格前，有人正在算未来会赔多少钱
scene: 保险公司年底盘点，办公室里表格摞得半人高，有人还在核对新产品的费率。 The actuary recalculated the premiums for the new policy.
sceneCN: 这里 actuary 是「精算师」（第 1 个义项：用统计方法计算保险风险与保费的专业人员）；句意为精算师重新核算了新保单的保费。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「精算的；保险精算的」
由本词构成的复合说法，义为「精算学」

senses.title: Insurance risk professional
senses.definition: a professional who computes insurance risks, premiums, and reserves with statistics
senses.definitionCN: 用统计方法计算保险风险、保费与准备金的专业人员
senses.example: The actuary recalculated the premiums for the new policy.
senses.exampleCN: 精算师重新核算了新保单的保费。
senses.why: Latin actuarius was a clerk who recorded accounts; the modern actuary still keeps the accounts of future risk.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 actuarius 是记录账目的书记员；现代精算师仍在为未来的风险记账。

senses.title: Pension and fund adviser
senses.titleCN: 养老金与基金测算顾问
senses.definition: an expert who evaluates pension schemes and investment funds for long-term solvency
senses.definitionCN: 评估养老金计划与投资基金长期偿付能力的专家
senses.example: The firm's actuary advised closing the underfunded pension plan.
senses.exampleCN: 公司的精算师建议关闭资金不足的养老金计划。
senses.why: The same arithmetic of future risk extends beyond insurance to any fund that must not run dry.
senses.whyCN: 同一套未来风险的算术延伸到保险之外，用于任何不能坐吃山空的基金。

intro.en: Actuary goes back to Latin actuarius, 'a clerk of accounts', from actus, 'a doing, a record of proceedings'.
intro.cn: actuary 溯源自拉丁语 actuarius（记账书记员），来自 actus（行为、事务记录）。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ag- meant 'to drive, to do'.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ag- 意为「驱动、做」。

items.en: actus meant 'a doing, an official record'; actuarius was a keeper of such records.
items.cn: actus 意为「行为、公务记录」；actuarius 是保管这类记录的人。

items.en: English actuary first named a clerk of the law courts.
items.cn: 英语 actuary 最初指法院的书记员。

items.en: Insurance companies borrowed the title for their risk calculators.
items.cn: 保险公司借用这个头衔称呼风险计算人员。

items.en: Actuary is now a profession of statistics, finance, and insurance.
items.cn: 如今精算师是一个融合统计、金融与保险的职业。

note.en: The first group gathers words from the Latin agere family; the second gathers finance and risk professions.
note.cn: 第一组收来自拉丁语 agere 词族的词；第二组收金融与风险行业的职业名称。

entries.definition: The adjective for actuary-related calculation.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「精算的」。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'real, existing in fact'; from the same agere family, only spelling near.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「实际的」；与 actuary 同源，词义已分道。

entries.definition: A common phrase for statistical life-expectancy tables.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「精算表」，记录预期寿命等统计数据的表格。

entries.definition: A person or company that takes on insurance risk.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「承保人」，承担保险风险的一方。

entries.definition: An expert in statistical methods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「统计学家」。

entries.definition: A professional who examines accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「审计员」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the clerk-of-accounts root and the premium scene; the abstract hooks picture tables that see the future.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「记账书记员」词根与保费场景；抽象记忆点想象能看见未来的表格。

normal.en: Actuary comes from actuarius, a Latin clerk of accounts.
normal.cn: actuary 来自拉丁语 actuarius，记账书记员。

normal.en: Actuarial tables list life expectancy for pricing.
normal.cn: 精算表列出预期寿命，用于定价。

normal.en: The plural changes y to i: actuaries.
normal.cn: 复数把 y 变 i：actuaries。

normal.en: Actuarial science is the degree that trains actuaries.
normal.cn: 精算学是培养精算师的学位。

normal.en: Actual shares the Latin family but means 'real'.
normal.cn: actual 同属拉丁词族，但意为「实际的」。

abstract.en: Picture a clerk adding columns that reach into the future.
abstract.cn: 想象书记员算着一列列伸向未来的数字。

abstract.en: Picture a life table where every age has a price.
abstract.cn: 想象一张每个年龄都标着价格的寿命表。

abstract.en: Picture a dam keeper measuring tomorrow's rain.
abstract.cn: 想象守坝人在测算明天的降雨。

examples.en: The actuary recalculated the premiums for the new policy.
examples.cn: 精算师重新核算了新保单的保费。

examples.en: Skilled actuaries are in high demand at insurance firms.
examples.cn: 保险公司对熟练的精算师需求很大。

examples.en: The actuary warned that the fund would run out in twenty years.
examples.cn: 精算师警告该基金二十年内会耗尽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克丘里」——阿哥在丘（堆）数理赔账目的人，就是精算师。

root: 拉丁语 agere（做）→ actus（行为、公务记录）→ actuarius（记账书记员）；核心义是「替未来的风险记账的人」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from calculating insurance risks, to evaluating pensions and funds.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从计算保险风险，走到评估养老金与基金。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clerk of accounts whose columns reach into the future
core.cn: 核心意象：账目伸向未来的记账书记员

branches.en: The professional who prices insurance risk.
branches.cn: 为保险风险定价的专业人员。

branches.en: The adviser who tests whether a fund can last.
branches.cn: 检验基金能否长期维系的顾问。

branches.en: Both senses turn statistics into money decisions.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把统计变成金钱决策。

branches.en: The old clerk of records survives in both roles.
branches.cn: 古老的记账书记员在两种角色中都留存。

branches.en: Actuarial tables are the everyday tool of this sense.
branches.cn: 精算表是这个义项的日常工具。

intro.en: The word carries the Latin record-root act- with the agent ending -uary, and the family also gives actual and act.
intro.cn: 这个词带着拉丁语「记录」词根 act- 与施动词尾 -uary，词族还产出 actual 与 act。

latinIntro.en: Latin actus and actuarius are the direct ancestors recorded here.
latinIntro.cn: 这里记录的拉丁语 actus 与 actuarius 是直接祖先。

definition_zh: 极坏的；糟透的；深不见底的；极度糟糕的
definition_en: extremely bad or poor in quality, and in older use also meaning immeasurably deep
core_image: 一口望不到底的黑色竖井，井壁上连一丝光都抓不住
scene: 连续几场暴雨之后，球队在泥地里连丢五球，看台上的人陆续离场。 The coach called the team's abysmal defending unacceptable at this level.
sceneCN: 这里 abysmal 指表现糟糕到几乎没有底线（第 1 个义项：极差的质量）；句意为教练称球队糟糕透顶的防守在这个水平上不可接受。

pos.zh: 极坏的；糟透的；深不可测的

senses.title: Extremely bad in quality
senses.definition: so bad in quality that it seems to have no bottom or limit
senses.definitionCN: 质量差到几乎看不到底线
senses.example: The food at that restaurant was abysmal.
senses.exampleCN: 那家餐厅的饭菜糟糕透顶。
senses.why: The word began as a description of physical depth; speakers later moved the image from a deep pit to a deep failure.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原本描述物理上的深度；说话者后来把「深坑」的形象移到了「深重的失败」上。

senses.title: Immeasurably deep
senses.definition: of a place or opening, so deep that its bottom cannot be reached or seen
senses.definitionCN: 指某个空间或开口深到无法触及或看见底部
senses.example: The explorers stared into an abysmal crack in the ice.
senses.exampleCN: 探险者凝视着冰面上那道深不见底的裂缝。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense: the adjective simply said that something had the quality of an abyss.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的物理义：形容词只是说某物具有「深渊」的性质。

senses.title: Utter ignorance
senses.definition: a complete and hopeless lack of knowledge or understanding
senses.definitionCN: 知识或理解上彻底而无可救药的匮乏
senses.example: His abysmal ignorance of basic geography embarrassed the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 他对基础地理的极度无知让整个团队难堪。
senses.why: Knowledge is treated as a container: when it is empty all the way down, the emptiness is described as bottomless.
senses.whyCN: 知识被当成一个容器：当它从上到下都是空的，这种空缺就被说成「无底」。

senses.title: Deplorable conditions
senses.definition: living or working conditions that are shockingly poor
senses.definitionCN: 居住或工作条件差得令人震惊
senses.example: The workers endured abysmal conditions in the old factory.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们在旧工厂里忍受着恶劣的条件。
senses.why: The image shifts from an empty mind to an empty place, and the place is judged by how far below a decent standard it falls.
senses.whyCN: 形象从「空空的头脑」转到「空空的场所」，而判断标准是它低于体面水平有多远。

senses.title: The lowest standard
senses.definition: a level of achievement or service that is far below what is expected
senses.definitionCN: 成绩或服务远低于应有水准
senses.example: The report described the hospital's record keeping as abysmal.
senses.exampleCN: 报告称这家医院的病历记录水平极低。
senses.why: A standard is a line drawn across a scale; when results fall far below that line, the fall is pictured as a plunge into depth.
senses.whyCN: 标准是刻度上的一条线；当结果远低于这条线时，这种下坠就被想象成跌入深处。

senses.title: A profound failure
senses.definition: a failure so complete that it seems to have no recoverable bottom
senses.definitionCN: 失败得如此彻底，仿佛没有可以重新站立的底部
senses.example: The launch was an abysmal failure and cost the firm its reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 这次发布是一次惨重失败，让公司失去了声誉。
senses.why: Failure is felt as a fall; the deeper the fall, the harder it is to climb back, so the word supplies the sense of no return.
senses.whyCN: 失败被感受为一次坠落；落得越深越难爬回，因此这个词带上了「无法回头」的意味。

senses.title: Miserable weather or setting
senses.definition: weather or surroundings that are bleak, wet and thoroughly unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 天气或环境阴冷潮湿、令人极不愉快
senses.example: We spent the holiday in abysmal rain and never left the hotel.
senses.exampleCN: 我们整个假期都困在恶劣的阴雨里，始终没离开旅馆。
senses.why: The physical sense survives in descriptions of landscape: a grey sky and endless rain feel like a pit without a bottom.
senses.whyCN: 物理义在景物描写中保留下来：灰暗的天空和无休止的雨，感觉就像一口没有底的深坑。

senses.title: The abyss itself, in old use
senses.definition: in older writing, the bottomless void or the underworld imagined as a pit
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的文本中，指无底的虚空或被想象成深坑的冥界
senses.example: Milton's lines place chaos in an abysmal region below the world.
senses.exampleCN: 弥尔顿的诗句把混沌放在世界之下一个深渊般的区域。
senses.why: Before the adjective meant poor quality, it described the abyss of early cosmology, a place with no floor and no limit.
senses.whyCN: 在形容词表示「质量差」之前，它描述的是早期宇宙观中的深渊：一个没有底、没有边界的所在。

intro.en: Abysmal belongs to the old imagery of a bottomless pit. It first described physical depth and only later became a word for very poor quality.
intro.cn: abysmal 属于「无底深坑」这一古老意象。它最初描述物理深度，后来才变成表示质量极差的词。

items.en: From the 19c. the adjective is applied figuratively to failures and conditions, and by the 20c. 'very bad' is the dominant sense in speech.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个形容词被比喻性地用于失败与境况；到二十世纪，「极差」已成为口语中的主导义。

items.en: Late Latin abysmalis and abyssimus were formed from abyssus, the Latin church word for the bottomless deep of Genesis.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 abysmalis 与 abyssimus 由 abyssus 构成，后者是拉丁教会在《创世记》中用来指无底深渊的词。

items.en: Greek abyssos meant 'bottomless, unfathomable', used of the sea and of the deep in early Christian writing.
items.cn: 希腊语 abyssos 意为「无底的、不可测的」，早期基督教文献用它指大海与深渊。

items.en: The Greek word is a- 'not, without' plus byssos 'depth, bottom'. The same byssos later gave English byssal, a term for a fine thread.
items.cn: 这个希腊词由 a-「无、没有」加 byssos「深度、底部」构成。同一个 byssos 后来还产生了英语 byssal，指细丝。

items.en: English took the word through Latin translations of the Bible, so abyss and abysmal entered the language with a theological charge before they became everyday intensifiers.
items.cn: 英语经由《圣经》的拉丁译本吸收此词，因此 abyss 与 abysmal 进入英语时带着神学色彩，之后才成为日常的强调词。

note.en: The first group shares letters or a root with abysmal; the second group shares the idea of being very bad.
note.cn: 第一组与 abysmal 共享字母或词根；第二组共享「非常糟糕」这一含义。

entries.definition: the bottomless deep; a very deep hole. It is the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 无底的深渊；极深的洞。它是这个形容词背后的名词。

entries.definition: relating to the deepest ocean zone, not to bad quality.
entries.definitionCN: 与最深的海域有关，与质量差无关。

entries.definition: in an extremely bad way. It adds the adverb ending to the same adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 以极差的方式。它在同一个形容词后加副词词尾。

entries.definition: an older spelling of abyss, now rare in ordinary text.
entries.definitionCN: abyss 的旧拼写，现代普通文本已罕见。

entries.definition: shockingly bad or cruel; often used of behaviour or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 骇人地糟糕或残忍；常用于行为或质量。

entries.definition: extremely bad or unpleasant, in a milder everyday tone.
entries.definitionCN: 极坏或极不愉快，语气在日常中稍轻。

entries.definition: so bad that it causes shock and disgust.
entries.definitionCN: 差到令人震惊和厌恶。

entries.definition: bleak, gloomy and poor in quality, often of conditions or results.
entries.definitionCN: 阴郁、黯淡且质量差，常指境况或结果。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the spelling to the image of a pit with no floor.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些联想把拼写和「没有底的深坑」这一形象连起来。

normal.en: abyss plus al: an abyss is a bottomless pit, so abysmal means as bad as a pit with no floor.
normal.cn: abyss 加 al：abyss 是无底深坑，所以 abysmal 就是「差得像没有底的坑」。

normal.en: Think of the letters a-b-y-s-s: a, by, ss, a fall that never stops.
normal.cn: 记字母 a-b-y-s-s：a、by、ss，像一次停不下来的下坠。

normal.en: A bad score is a fall; an abysmal score is a fall with no bottom.
normal.cn: 差分数是一次下坠；abysmal 的分数是看不到底的下坠。

normal.en: Say abysmal slowly: the stress falls on the second syllable, like a stone dropping.
normal.cn: 慢慢读 abysmal：重音落在第二个音节，像石头往下掉。

normal.en: Link it with the noun abyss you already know from geography texts.
normal.cn: 把它和地理课本里学过的名词 abyss 联系起来。

abstract.en: Depth becomes value: the deeper the failure, the lower the quality.
abstract.cn: 深度变成价值：失败越深，质量越低。

abstract.en: A container image: an empty mind all the way down is bottomless ignorance.
abstract.cn: 容器意象：从上到下都空的头脑，就是无底的无知。

abstract.en: No floor means no recovery, which is why the word feels stronger than merely bad.
abstract.cn: 没有底就意味着无法恢复，所以这个词比单纯的 bad 更有力。

examples.en: The team's abysmal defending cost them the match.
examples.cn: 球队糟糕透顶的防守让他们输掉了比赛。

examples.en: Living conditions in the camp were abysmal.
examples.cn: 营地里的生活条件极其恶劣。

examples.en: He showed an abysmal lack of preparation for the interview.
examples.cn: 他在面试中表现出极度的准备不足。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 abyss（深渊）加 -al 记成「深到没底」，再引申为「差到没底」。

root: 希腊语 abyssos（无底深渊）：a-（无）+ byssos（深度）

sensesIntro.en: Abysmal has one physical core, depth without a bottom, and several figurative extensions in which that depth measures failure, ignorance or poor conditions.
sensesIntro.cn: abysmal 只有一个物理核心，即「没有底的深度」，其余义项都是引申：用这种深度来衡量失败、无知或恶劣条件。

core.en: A PIT WITH NO BOTTOM
core.cn: 一口没有底的深坑

branches.en: Depth itself, first physical and then figurative.
branches.cn: 先是物理深度，随后转为比喻性的深。

branches.en: Emptiness all the way down becomes extreme ignorance.
branches.cn: 从上到下的空缺变成极度的无知。

branches.en: A place or setting judged to be far below a decent level.
branches.cn: 场所或环境被判定远低于体面水平。

branches.en: A standard missed so badly that the result is a deep failure.
branches.cn: 严重未达标准，结果成为深重的失败。

branches.en: The old cosmological abyss, kept in literary description.
branches.cn: 古老的宇宙论深渊，保留在文学描写中。

intro.en: The word is built from a Greek negative prefix, a Greek root for depth, and an English adjective ending.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个希腊否定前缀、一个表示深度的希腊词根和一个英语形容词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin and Greek entries show how the idea travelled from sea depth to church language and then to English.
latinIntro.cn: 下面这些拉丁语与希腊语条目展示这一概念如何从海洋深度进入教会语言，再进入英语。

items.meaning: without a bottom, hence extremely deep or bad
items.meaningCN: 没有底，因而极深或极坏

items.example: The ship sank into the abyss.

items.meaning: relating to the abyss or the deep sea
items.example: Abyssal creatures live far below the surface.
items.exampleCN: 深海生物生活在海面以下很远的地方。

items.example: The old poem speaks of an abysm of fire.
items.exampleCN: 那首古老的诗提到火焰的深渊。

items.meaning: relating to, having the quality of

latinEntries.meaning: bottomless deep, the deep of scripture
latinEntries.meaningCN: 无底的深处，经文中的深渊

definition_zh: 使动作；开动（机器）；驱使（人行动）
definition_en: to make a machine work, or to cause someone to act in a certain way
core_image: 按下开关，齿轮咔哒一声转起来
scene: 老式电梯要通电了，工人把手柄一扳，缆绳立刻绷紧。 A lever actuates the safety brake when the cable snaps.
sceneCN: 这里 actuate 是「使动作、触发」（第 1 个义项：让机械装置开始工作）；句意为缆绳断裂时连杆会触发安全制动。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「启动；驱动」
由本词加施动后缀构成，义为「执行器；促动器」

senses.title: To set a mechanism in motion
senses.definition: to put a machine or device into action
senses.definitionCN: 让机器或装置开始运作
senses.example: A lever actuates the safety brake when the cable snaps.
senses.exampleCN: 缆绳断裂时连杆会触发安全制动。
senses.why: Latin agere meant 'to drive'; actuate is to drive a thing into doing its work.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 agere 意为「驱动」；actuate 就是把一件东西驱入它的工作状态。

senses.title: To motivate a person to act
senses.definition: to be the inner cause of someone's behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 成为某人行为的内在动因
senses.example: She was actuated by loyalty, not by hope of reward.
senses.exampleCN: 驱使她的是忠诚，而不是报酬的希望。
senses.why: The same driving force applied to a person becomes motive; the mind is the machine being switched on.
senses.whyCN: 同一股驱动力作用到人身上就成了动机；心智就是那台被按下开关的机器。

intro.en: Actuate joins Latin actus, 'a doing', with the verb ending -ate, 'to make'.
intro.cn: actuate 把拉丁语 actus（行为）与动词词尾 -ate（使）结合。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ag- meant 'to drive, to do'.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ag- 意为「驱动、做」。

items.en: actus meant 'a doing, a driving'.
items.cn: actus 意为「行为、驱动」。

items.en: actuare meant 'to put into action'.
items.cn: actuare 意为「使付诸行动」。

items.en: English actuate was first used of machines and springs.
items.cn: 英语 actuate 最初用于机器与弹簧。

items.en: Technical use survives in actuators; the 'motivate' sense is now formal.
items.cn: 技术用法保留在 actuator 一词中；「驱使」义如今偏正式。

note.en: The first group gathers the agere family and its offspring; the second gathers verbs of setting things or people in motion.
note.cn: 第一组收 agere 词族及其派生词；第二组收让物或人动起来的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of triggering a device.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「启动、触发」。

entries.definition: The device that carries out the triggering, common in engineering.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「执行器」，工程常用。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'real'; spelling near, meaning far.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「实际的」；拼写相近，意义不同。

entries.definition: To set off a device or a chain of events.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「触发、引发」。

entries.definition: To make a system or plan start working.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「激活、使生效」。

entries.definition: To drive a person forward by force or motive.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「驱使、推动（人）」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the drive-root act- and the engineering word actuator; the abstract hooks picture a lever thrown.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「驱动」词根 act- 与工程词 actuator；抽象记忆点想象扳动连杆。

normal.en: Actuate is act- plus -ate: to put into act.
normal.cn: actuate 是 act- 加 -ate：使之进入行动。

normal.en: An actuator is the part that actuates a machine.
normal.cn: actuator 是执行 actuate 的部件。

normal.en: Be actuated by is the formal pattern for motives.
normal.cn: be actuated by 是表示动机的正式结构。

normal.en: Activate is the everyday word; actuate is technical.
normal.cn: activate 是日常用词，actuate 偏技术。

normal.en: The noun is actuation.
normal.cn: 名词是 actuation。

abstract.en: Picture a hand throwing a big brass lever.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扳下黄铜大连杆。

abstract.en: Picture gears waking up one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象齿轮被一个个唤醒。

abstract.en: Picture conscience pressing the start button of a decision.
abstract.cn: 想象良知按下决定的启动键。

examples.en: A lever actuates the safety brake when the cable snaps.
examples.cn: 缆绳断裂时连杆会触发安全制动。

examples.en: The relay actuates the alarm circuit within milliseconds.
examples.cn: 继电器在几毫秒内接通报警电路。

examples.en: He was actuated by a desire to defend his colleagues.
examples.cn: 驱使他的是保护同事的愿望。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克丘诶特」——阿克一按开关，丘（机器）就哎哟一声动起来，就是驱动。

root: 拉丁语 agere（驱动）→ actus（行为）→ actuare（使行动）；核心义是「把驱动之柄按下，使人或机器行动」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from setting a machine in motion, to driving a person's motive.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从使机器运作，走到驱动人的动机。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lever thrown, gears turning
core.cn: 核心意象：连杆扳下，齿轮转动

branches.en: The mechanical start of a device.
branches.cn: 装置的机械性启动。

branches.en: The hidden cause behind a person's action.
branches.cn: 人行为背后的内在动因。

branches.en: Machine and mind share the same switch.
branches.cn: 机器与心智共用同一个开关。

branches.en: Engineering keeps this sense alive in actuator.
branches.cn: 工程学在 actuator 中保留了这个义项。

branches.en: Both senses come from the Latin idea of driving.
branches.cn: 两个义项都来自拉丁语「驱动」的观念。

intro.en: The verb joins the Latin root act- with the causative ending -ate, and the family adds nouns and the everyday activate.
intro.cn: 这个动词把拉丁语词根 act- 与使动词尾 -ate 结合，词族另加名词与日常词 activate。

latinIntro.en: Latin actus and actuare are the recorded ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 记录在案的拉丁语祖先为 actus 与 actuare。

definition_zh: 岩石圈；由地壳与上地幔顶部组成的刚性外壳
definition_en: the rigid outer shell of a planet, made of the crust and the uppermost mantle
core_image: 一颗石球外面套着一层薄而坚硬的石壳，壳上裂成几块大板
scene: 岩石圈并不整体移动，它早已裂成几块大板。 The lithosphere is broken into large plates that move slowly over the softer layer below.
sceneCN: 这里 lithosphere 指「岩石圈」（第 1 个义项：地壳与上地幔顶部组成的刚性外壳）；句意为岩石圈裂成几块大板，在下面较软的层之上缓慢移动。

pos.zh: 岩石圈（地壳与上地幔顶部的刚性部分）

senses.title: The rigid outer shell of a planet
senses.titleCN: 岩石圈：行星的刚性外壳
senses.definition: the rigid outer shell of a planet, made of the crust and the uppermost mantle
senses.definitionCN: 由地壳与上地幔顶部组成的行星刚性外壳
senses.example: The lithosphere is broken into large plates that move slowly over the softer layer below.
senses.exampleCN: 岩石圈裂成几块大板，在下面较软的层之上缓慢移动。
senses.why: The word joins Greek lithos 'stone' with sphaira 'sphere', so it names the stone sphere around a planet.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把希腊语 lithos「石头」与 sphaira「球」合在一起，指行星外面那层石头球壳。

senses.title: The layer that carries the plates
senses.definition: the layer whose fragments are the tectonic plates
senses.definitionCN: 其碎块构成构造板块的那一层
senses.example: Each plate is a piece of lithosphere, not a separate sheet of crust.
senses.exampleCN: 每个板块都是岩石圈的一块，而不是单独的一层地壳。
senses.why: Plates are defined mechanically: they are the pieces of the rigid shell, so the shell and the plates are the same material at different scales.
senses.whyCN: 板块是按力学性质界定的：它们是刚性外壳的碎块，所以外壳与板块是同一材料在不同尺度上的说法。

senses.title: Thickness that varies by setting
senses.definition: the part of the shell whose thickness differs under oceans and continents
senses.definitionCN: 这层外壳在海洋之下与大陆之下厚度不同
senses.example: Continental lithosphere can be several times thicker than oceanic lithosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆岩石圈的厚度可以达到大洋岩石圈的好几倍。
senses.why: Old, cold continental roots extend far deeper than young oceanic plates, so the same shell has very different depths.
senses.whyCN: 古老寒冷的大陆根扎得远比年轻的大洋板块深，因此同一层外壳的深度差别很大。

senses.title: Rigid, elastic behaviour
senses.definition: the mechanical property of bending and breaking rather than flowing
senses.definitionCN: 会弯曲、会断裂而不会流动的力学性质
senses.example: The lithosphere bends elastically under the weight of a volcano.
senses.exampleCN: 火山的重压使岩石圈发生弹性弯曲。
senses.why: The key contrast is with the asthenosphere: over long times the shell behaves as a solid, while the layer below can flow.
senses.whyCN: 关键对照是与软流圈的区别：在长时间尺度上这层外壳表现为固体，而下面的层可以流动。

senses.title: The layer above the asthenosphere
senses.definition: the outer shell defined by its position above the weaker asthenosphere
senses.definitionCN: 以位于较软弱的软流圈之上来界定的外壳
senses.example: The boundary between lithosphere and asthenosphere is a change in strength, not in rock type.
senses.exampleCN: 岩石圈与软流圈的界线是强度的变化，而不是岩石种类的变化。
senses.why: The same rock can belong to either layer; what changes across the boundary is how easily it deforms.
senses.whyCN: 同一种岩石可以属于这两层中的任一层；跨过界线改变的是它变形的难易程度。

senses.title: A planetary shell beyond Earth
senses.titleCN: 地球之外的行星岩石圈
senses.definition: the equivalent rigid shell of another rocky planet or moon
senses.definitionCN: 其他岩石行星或卫星的同类刚性外壳
senses.example: Mars has a thick lithosphere that has barely moved for billions of years.
senses.exampleCN: 火星的岩石圈很厚，数十亿年间几乎没怎么移动。
senses.why: The term is defined by mechanics, so it transfers to any rocky body with a stiff outer layer.
senses.whyCN: 这个术语按力学性质定义，因此可推广到任何具有坚硬外层的岩石天体。

senses.title: The host of resources and earthquakes
senses.definition: the layer in which most mines, oil fields and shallow earthquakes occur
senses.definitionCN: 大多数矿山、油田与浅源地震所在的层
senses.example: Most earthquakes begin within the lithosphere, where rock is brittle enough to break.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数地震始于岩石圈内，那里的岩石足够脆，会断裂。
senses.why: Brittle failure requires a stiff material, so the rigid shell is where faults slip and where resources are dug out.
senses.whyCN: 脆性破坏需要坚硬的材料，因此断层在这层刚性外壳里滑动，资源也从这里开采。

senses.title: The object of lithospheric study
senses.definition: the shell as a subject of geophysics, geochemistry and plate reconstruction
senses.definitionCN: 作为地球物理、地球化学与板块重建研究对象的这层外壳
senses.example: Lithospheric studies combine seismic imaging with heat-flow measurements.
senses.exampleCN: 岩石圈研究把地震成像与热流测量结合起来。
senses.why: Once a layer is named, it becomes a research object with its own methods and its own adjective, lithospheric.
senses.whyCN: 一层一旦被命名，就成为有自己方法和形容词 lithospheric 的研究对象。

intro.en: Lithosphere is a scientific compound coined from two Greek nouns. The parts are transparent and the meaning has stayed stable since the term was formed. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: lithosphere 是由两个希腊名词构成的科学复合词。构词成分清楚，术语形成以来含义一直稳定。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek lithos meant 'stone', and sphaira meant 'ball, sphere'; both are common in scientific compounds.
items.cn: 希腊语 lithos 意为「石头」，sphaira 意为「球、球体」；两者在科学复合词中都很常见。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geologists needed a name for the solid outer shell of the planet and combined the two Greek nouns.
items.cn: 十九世纪的地质学家需要给行星的固体外壳命名，就把这两个希腊名词组合起来。

items.en: The English term spread with the growth of geophysics; its modern definition depends on strength, not on chemical composition.
items.cn: 这个英语术语随地球物理的发展而传播；它的现代定义取决于力学强度，而不是化学成分。

items.en: Plate tectonics gave the word a central role: the lithosphere is the layer that breaks into plates and slides over the asthenosphere.
items.cn: 板块构造学说赋予这个词核心地位：岩石圈就是裂成板块并在软流圈上滑动的那一层。

items.en: The paired term asthenosphere was coined later to name the weaker layer below, so the two words are defined against each other.
items.cn: 与之配套的术语 asthenosphere 后来才出现，用来命名下面较软弱的层，因此这两个词是相互对照定义的。

note.en: Group one collects the other -sphere words that are constantly mixed up; group two collects the geological units that sit next to lithosphere in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是极易混淆的其他 -sphere 词；第二组是语义上与岩石圈相邻的地质单位。

entries.definition: the envelope of gases around a planet. It shares the -sphere ending but begins with a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 行星周围的气体层。它共享 -sphere 结尾，但开头是另一个词根。

entries.definition: the zone where living things exist. The first element is Greek bios 'life', not lithos 'stone'.
entries.definitionCN: 生物生存的圈层。前半部分是希腊语 bios「生命」，不是 lithos「石头」。

entries.definition: all the water on a planet. The first element is Greek hydor 'water'.
entries.definitionCN: 行星上的全部水体。前半部分是希腊语 hydor「水」。

entries.definition: a print made by lithography. It shares litho- 'stone' but ends with -graph 'write', not -sphere.
entries.definitionCN: 石版印刷品。它共享 litho-「石头」，但结尾是 -graph「写」，不是 -sphere。

entries.definition: the outermost rocky skin of a planet, thinner than the lithosphere and included within it.
entries.definitionCN: 行星最外面的岩石薄壳，比岩石圈薄，并且包含在岩石圈之内。

entries.definition: one large piece of the lithosphere that moves as a unit.
entries.definitionCN: 岩石圈中作为整体运动的一大块。

entries.definition: the weaker layer beneath the lithosphere, which can flow slowly.
entries.definitionCN: 岩石圈之下较软弱、可以缓慢流动的层。

entries.definition: any outer covering; it describes the shape but carries no geological definition.
entries.definitionCN: 任何外壳；它只描述形状，不含地质学定义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek roots and real layer names, so each word can be decoded rather than merely rhymed.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词根与真实的圈层名称，因此每个词可以拆解，而不是只靠押韵。

normal.en: litho- means stone and -sphere means ball, so lithosphere is the stone ball around a planet.
normal.cn: litho- 表示石头，-sphere 表示球，所以 lithosphere 就是行星外面那层石头球壳。

normal.en: The four -sphere words form a set: atmosphere is air, hydrosphere is water, biosphere is life, lithosphere is stone.
normal.cn: 四个 -sphere 词构成一组：atmosphere 是气，hydrosphere 是水，biosphere 是生命，lithosphere 是石头。

normal.en: The lithosphere is the plate itself; the crust is only its top layer, so a plate is thicker than a crust.
normal.cn: 岩石圈就是板块本身；地壳只是它的最上层，所以板块比地壳厚。

normal.en: The boundary with the asthenosphere is a strength boundary, not a rock-type boundary.
normal.cn: 与软流圈的界线是强度界线，不是岩石种类界线。

normal.en: Earthquakes and mines cluster in the lithosphere because brittle rock breaks and holds ore.
normal.cn: 地震与矿山集中在岩石圈，因为脆性岩石会断裂，也能储存矿石。

abstract.en: Abstractly, the lithosphere is a cracked eggshell: hard, thin, and divided into pieces that can slide.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，岩石圈像一层裂开的蛋壳：坚硬、很薄，并分成可以滑动的碎块。

abstract.en: The image pairs hardness with thinness: what makes it a plate is that it can break rather than flow.
abstract.cn: 这个形象把「硬」与「薄」配在一起：使它成为板块的，正是它会断裂而不是流动。

abstract.en: Symbol: a thin hard ring around a soft inner circle, with cracks across the ring.
abstract.cn: 符号：软内圈外面套一层薄硬的环，环上布满裂缝。

examples.en: Oceanic lithosphere is created at mid-ocean ridges and destroyed at trenches.
examples.cn: 大洋岩石圈在大洋中脊生成，在海沟处消亡。

examples.en: The lithosphere behaves as a rigid plate over long time spans.
examples.cn: 在长时间尺度上，岩石圈表现为刚性板块。

examples.en: Scientists map the base of the lithosphere using seismic waves.
examples.cn: 科学家用地震波绘制岩石圈的底部。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里索斯菲尔」—— 石头（litho）做的球（sphere） → lithosphere 岩石圈

root: 由希腊语 lithos（石头）与 sphaira（球）组合而成，字面义为「石头球壳」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of lithosphere. The thread is a hard outer shell: it carries the plates, bends elastically, and sits on a softer layer.
sensesIntro.cn: lithosphere 的八个义项。主线是一层坚硬外壳：它承载板块、发生弹性弯曲，并坐在较软的层之上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin hard shell around a soft interior, cracked into moving pieces.
core.cn: 核心意象：软内部外面一层薄硬壳，壳裂成会移动的碎块。

branches.en: SHELL AND THICKNESS: the same hard shell is thin under oceans and thick under old continents.
branches.cn: 外壳与厚度：同一层硬壳在海洋下很薄，在古老大陆下很厚。

branches.en: PLATE IDENTITY: a plate is not a separate crust but a fragment of this shell.
branches.cn: 板块同一性：板块不是另一层地壳，而是这层外壳的碎块。

branches.en: STRENGTH BOUNDARY: rigidity is measured against the softer layer below.
branches.cn: 强度界线：刚性是相对于下面较软的层来衡量的。

branches.en: PLANETARY TRANSFER: the mechanical definition works on any rocky body.
branches.cn: 行星推广：这一定义按力学性质成立，因此适用于任何岩石天体。

branches.en: HUMAN USE: the same shell holds ore, breaks in earthquakes and becomes an object of study.
branches.cn: 人类利用：同一层外壳储存矿石、在地震中破裂，也成为研究对象。

intro.en: Lithosphere is a compound of two Greek nouns, and both parts recur across scientific English, so the word is easy to decode and easy to extend.
intro.cn: lithosphere 由两个希腊名词复合而成，两部分在科学英语中反复出现，因此这个词既好拆解也便于扩展。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here: the elements are Greek lithos and sphaira, combined in modern scientific coinage, so latinEntries is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语来源：构词成分是希腊语 lithos 与 sphaira，在现代科技术语中组合而成，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.example: Lithology is the study of rock types.
The atmosphere is the gaseous sphere of a planet.
items.exampleCN: 大气层是行星的气体圈层。

items.meaningCN: 与岩石圈有关的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.example: Lithospheric plates move a few centimetres a year.
items.exampleCN: 岩石圈板块每年移动几厘米。

items.meaningCN: 岩石类型研究（-logy 表示学科）
items.example: The drill core changed lithology at two hundred metres.
items.exampleCN: 钻芯在两百米处岩性发生变化。

items.meaningCN: 使沉积物变成岩石（-ify 表示使成为）
items.example: Pressure and cementation lithify loose sand.
items.exampleCN: 压力与胶结作用把松砂变成岩石。

items.meaning: made of stone; relating to stone
items.example: Archaeologists found lithic tools in the cave.
items.exampleCN: 考古学家在洞中发现了石制工具。

items.meaning: a rigid fragment of the lithosphere
items.meaningCN: 岩石圈的一块刚性碎块
items.example: Each lithosphere plate carries both crust and upper mantle.
items.exampleCN: 每个岩石圈板块都带着地壳与上地幔。

items.meaning: the depth where the rigid shell meets the weaker layer
items.meaningCN: 刚性外壳与较软层相接的深度（复合术语）
items.example: The lithosphere-asthenosphere boundary lies near one hundred kilometres under oceans.
items.exampleCN: 大洋之下的岩石圈与软流圈界面约在一百公里深处。

definition_zh: 渗透；潜移默化；逐渐吸收
definition_en: the slow passing of something through a thin boundary, or the quiet way a person takes in what surrounds him
core_image: 水隔着薄薄一层膜慢慢渗过去，到最后两边一样咸
scene: 他在那间厨房待了三年，没学过菜谱，手艺却自己长了出来。 He spent three years in that kitchen and never studied a recipe, yet the craft came to him by osmosis.
sceneCN: 这里 osmosis 指潜移默化的吸收（第 2 个义项：潜移默化的学习）；句意为他在厨房待了三年，没学菜谱，手艺却自己长了出来。

pos.zh: 渗透；潜移默化；逐渐吸收

senses.title: Physical osmosis
senses.definition: the movement of a liquid through a thin membrane toward the stronger solution
senses.definitionCN: 液体穿过薄膜、流向浓度更高一侧的运动
senses.example: Water crossed the membrane by osmosis until both sides matched.
senses.exampleCN: 水靠渗透穿过薄膜，直到两侧浓度相同。
senses.why: The core picture is a wall that water can pass but salt cannot.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面是一堵水能过、盐不能过的墙。

senses.title: Absorbing knowledge quietly
senses.definition: taking in a skill or body of knowledge by being near it rather than by study
senses.definitionCN: 靠身处其中而不是靠研习来吸收技能或知识
senses.example: He learned the kitchen by osmosis, watching and never asking.
senses.exampleCN: 他靠耳濡目染学会厨房里的活，只是看，从不问。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the membrane: knowledge crosses a boundary without being poured.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了那层膜：知识穿过边界，而不是被灌进去。

senses.title: Passive uptake
senses.definition: receiving an attitude or habit without choosing to
senses.definitionCN: 未经选择地接收一种态度或习惯
senses.example: She absorbed the family's caution by osmosis and never noticed.
senses.exampleCN: 她不知不觉吸收了家里的谨慎，自己从未察觉。
senses.why: Here the word describes what happens when nobody is teaching.
senses.whyCN: 这里描述的是没有人在教时发生的事。

senses.title: Diffusion of ideas
senses.definition: the gradual spread of an idea through a group until it seems native there
senses.definitionCN: 观念在群体中逐渐扩散，直到像本来就长在那里
senses.example: The new vocabulary entered the office by osmosis, one meeting at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 新词汇靠渗透进入办公室，一次会议渗一点。
senses.why: Groups, like membranes, let some things through faster than others.
senses.whyCN: 群体像膜一样，让某些东西过得比别人快。

senses.title: Subtle influence
senses.definition: the slow permeation of a place or person by an outside influence
senses.definitionCN: 外来影响缓慢渗入一个地方或一个人
senses.example: The city changed by osmosis, street by street, without a single decree.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市靠浸润改变，一条街一条街地变，没有一道法令。
senses.why: The word is useful when no cause can be pointed to, only a drift.
senses.whyCN: 当指不出原因、只看到漂移时，这个词就派上用场。

senses.title: Biological membrane exchange
senses.definition: the exchange of water and solutes across cell membranes in living tissue
senses.definitionCN: 活组织中水与溶质跨细胞膜的交换
senses.example: Roots depend on osmosis to pull water from the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 根靠渗透从土壤里吸水。
senses.why: Biology uses the word literally, and the metaphor borrows its patience.
senses.whyCN: 生物学按字面使用这个词，比喻借走的是它的耐心。

senses.title: Social assimilation
senses.definition: the process by which a newcomer slowly takes on a group's ways
senses.definitionCN: 新来者慢慢接受一个群体行事方式的过程
senses.example: The new clerk was assimilated by osmosis long before the training ended.
senses.exampleCN: 新职员在培训结束前很久就已经被同化了。
senses.why: People, too, are semi-permeable; the group enters by degrees.
senses.whyCN: 人也是半透的；群体是一点一点进来的。

senses.title: Doing something without knowing how
senses.definition: the casual phrase for knowing a thing one was never formally taught
senses.definitionCN: 对未曾正式学过却会做某事的一种随口说法
senses.example: Ask him the rule and he cannot tell you; he knows it by osmosis.
senses.exampleCN: 问他规则他说不出来；他是不知不觉学会的。
senses.why: Used loosely, the word admits that the learning had no syllabus.
senses.whyCN: 松散用法下，这个词承认这份学习没有教学大纲。

intro.en: Osmosis was coined by nineteenth-century science from a Greek word for a push: the liquid is not poured, it is pressed through.
intro.cn: osmosis 由十九世纪科学用一个意为「推」的希腊词造出：液体不是被倒过去，而是被推过去。

items.en: Osmos meant 'a push, an impulse', the pressure that starts the movement.
items.cn: osmos 意为「推、冲动」，是启动这一运动的压力。

items.en: The suffix -osis named a process or condition, as in osmosis or diagnosis.
items.cn: 后缀 -osis 命名一种过程或状态，如 osmosis 与 diagnosis。

items.en: Nineteenth-century chemists needed a word for water rising through a membrane, and built it from these pieces.
items.cn: 十九世纪化学家需要为水穿过薄膜上升的现象造词，便用了这两个部件。

items.en: The word stayed technical until teachers borrowed it for learning that happens without lessons.
items.cn: 这个词一直技术化，直到教师们借它来描述没有课程的学习。

items.en: Today 'by osmosis' is a common phrase for absorbing a culture, an accent or a habit.
items.cn: 今天 by osmosis 是常用说法，指吸收一种文化、口音或习惯。

note.en: The look-alike group is the osm- family; the near-meaning group separates diffusion, permeation and plain absorption.
note.cn: 形近组是 osm- 词族；近义组把「扩散」「渗入」与「吸收」分开。

entries.definition: more than one instance of osmosis.
entries.definitionCN: 多次渗透过程。

entries.definition: relating to osmosis.
entries.definitionCN: 与渗透有关的。

entries.definition: by means of osmosis.
entries.definitionCN: 以渗透方式。

entries.definition: to pass or absorb by osmosis.
entries.definitionCN: 渗透；逐渐吸收。

entries.definition: the spreading of particles or ideas.
entries.definitionCN: 粒子或观念的散布。

entries.definition: the passing through a material.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过某种材料的渗入。

entries.definition: the taking in of something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物的吸收。

entries.definition: a slow entry into a group or place.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢进入某群体或场所。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of water rising through a thin skin until both sides are the same.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「水穿过一层薄皮上升，直到两边一样」的画面。

normal.en: Osmosis starts with osmos, a push: nothing is poured, everything is pressed.
normal.cn: osmosis 起于 osmos（推）：没有被倒进去的东西，全是被推进去的。

normal.en: Think of a bladder of brine in fresh water, slowly swelling.
normal.cn: 想象一只装盐水的囊泡放在淡水里，慢慢胀起来。

normal.en: Oz-mosis: the first syllable sounds like 'oz', a slow drip through a wall.
normal.cn: oz-mosis：第一个音节像 oz，一滴一滴穿过墙。

normal.en: Say oz-MOH-sis; the long o is the slow part of the process.
normal.cn: 读成 oz-MOH-sis，那个长 o 就是过程中慢的那一段。

normal.en: Pair it with by: things learned by osmosis were never formally taught.
normal.cn: 把它和 by 配对：by osmosis 学到的东西从不曾被正式教授。

abstract.en: Osmosis is how a culture gets into a person without a lesson plan.
abstract.cn: 潜移默化是文化不经课程就进入一个人的方式。

abstract.en: The membrane matters: what passes is not everything, only what the wall allows.
abstract.cn: 膜是要紧的：过的不是全部，只是墙允许的那部分。

abstract.en: Slow is the point; anything fast enough to notice is called teaching.
abstract.cn: 慢是重点；快到能被注意到的，就叫教学。

examples.en: He spent three years in that kitchen and the craft came to him by osmosis.
examples.cn: 他在厨房待了三年，手艺不知不觉就长了出来。

examples.en: Water crossed the membrane by osmosis until both sides matched.
examples.cn: 水靠渗透穿过薄膜，直到两侧相同。

examples.en: The new vocabulary entered the office by osmosis, one meeting at a time.
examples.cn: 新词汇靠潜移默化进入办公室，一次会议渗一点。

dict_mnemonic.text: os（推）+ mosis（过程）：水被推着穿过薄膜，就是「渗透」。

root: 希腊语 ōsmos（推、推动），十九世纪科学加 -osis 造出 osmosis

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all move something across a boundary: water through a membrane, a skill through a wall of habit, an idea through a group.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某物送过一道边界：水穿过膜、手艺穿过习惯的墙、观念穿过一个群体。

core.en: WATER CROSSING A THIN WALL
core.cn: 水穿过一层薄壁

branches.en: The literal passage of water in a lab and in a cell.
branches.cn: 实验室与细胞里水的字面通过。

branches.en: A skill taken in by nearness and an attitude taken in without choice.
branches.cn: 靠近而得的技能与无从选择而得的态度。

branches.en: An idea spreading through a group and an influence entering a city.
branches.cn: 观念穿过群体与影响进入城市。

branches.en: A newcomer slowly becoming one of the group.
branches.cn: 新来者慢慢成为群体一员。

branches.en: The loose phrase for knowing without having been taught.
branches.cn: 未曾受教却知道的松散说法。

intro.en: The osm- family is about pushing through: osmosis passes, osmotic describes the passing, endosmosis pushes in and exosmosis pushes out.
intro.cn: osm- 词族关乎推过去：osmosis 是过程，osmotic 描述这个过程，endosmosis 推入，exosmosis 推出。

latinIntro.en: Greek osmos is the push and -osis is the process; the prefixes endo- and exo- decide which side the water enters from.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 osmos 是那一下推，-osis 是过程；前缀 endo- 与 exo- 决定水从哪一边进。

items.example: The syrup osmosed into the fruit.
He needs dialysis twice a week.

definition_zh: 外交；外交实务；外交手腕；外交界；（喻）交际策略
definition_en: the conduct of relations between states through negotiation and contact, and the skill of managing such relations without giving offence
core_image: 长桌两侧各坐一人，桌上摊着几张对折的文书，桌下两双脚都没有后退
scene: 长桌两侧各坐一人，桌上摊着几张对折的文书，侍者退到门边，谁也没有先起身。 Quiet diplomacy kept the two delegations talking through the winter.
sceneCN: 这里 diplomacy 指「以持续谈判与往来处理国家间关系的实务」（第 1 个义项：通过接触而非武力处理对外关系的方式）；句意为静默外交让两个代表团在整个冬天都保持对话。图中可辨识物件：长桌、对折的文书、两侧的座椅、退到门边的侍者。

pos.zh: 外交；外交实务；外交手腕；外交界（不可数；指具体的外交活动时可数，复数 diplomacies）

forms.label: 复数（指多国的外交活动）

derivatives.zh: 外交官（由 diplomatic 逆构而来，语义由「外交的」收窄为执行外交的人）
外交的；圆融的（经法语 diplomatique，由拉丁 diploma 加关系后缀，语义由文书转到国家事务与分寸）
圆融地；以外交方式（diplomatic 加 -ly，语义由性质转为方式）
不圆融的；直来直去的（un- 加 diplomatic，语义加否定，指缺少分寸）
外交家；外交事务专家（diplomatic 加 -ist，旧式说法，语义由性质转为人与职业）
文凭；公文（希腊 diploma「对折的纸」，语义由折叠文书转到证书，与外交实务分道）

senses.title: The conduct of relations between states
senses.titleCN: 处理国家间关系的实务
senses.definition: the ongoing work of managing contact between governments through talks, representation and agreement rather than force
senses.definitionCN: 通过会谈、派驻代表与达成协议而非武力来处理政府之间往来的持续工作
senses.example: Quiet diplomacy kept the two delegations talking through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 静默外交让两个代表团在整个冬天都保持对话。
senses.why: The word names the business that credentials and envoys exist to carry on, so it points to the activity rather than to any one paper.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是凭证与使节存在的目的所指向的那项业务，因此指活动而非某一份纸页。

senses.title: The profession and the diplomatic service
senses.titleCN: 外交这一职业与外交界
senses.definition: the career, ranks and institutions of officials who represent a state abroad
senses.definitionCN: 在海外代表国家的官员所从事的职业、等级与机构
senses.example: She entered diplomacy after ten years in the foreign ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 她在外交部工作十年后进入了外交界。
senses.why: Once the activity is organized into a service with ranks, the name of the activity also names the career.
senses.whyCN: 当这项活动被组织成有等级的部门后，活动的名称也指这份职业。

senses.title: Skill in negotiation
senses.definition: the ability to trade concessions, time moves and read the other side in order to reach an agreement
senses.definitionCN: 通过交换让步、掌握时机与判断对方来达成协议的能力
senses.example: The deal was saved by patient diplomacy behind closed doors.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔交易靠闭门之后的耐心谈判手腕才得以挽回。
senses.why: The activity demands a craft, and the abstract noun soon named the craft itself rather than the institution.
senses.whyCN: 这项活动需要技艺，这个抽象名词很快便指技艺本身，而非机构。

senses.title: Tact in ordinary dealings
senses.titleCN: 日常处事中的圆融得体
senses.definition: the everyday skill of handling people and conflicts without giving offence
senses.definitionCN: 在日常中处理人际关系与冲突而不冒犯他人的能力
senses.example: It took diplomacy to tell him his proposal had already been rejected.
senses.exampleCN: 要告诉他提案早已被否决，是需要一点圆融的。
senses.why: Negotiators became the model of tact, so the noun moved from the conference room to the kitchen table.
senses.whyCN: 谈判者成了分寸的样板，于是这个名词从会议室走到了饭桌。

senses.title: Work in an embassy abroad
senses.definition: the daily duties of a mission, from visa interviews to reporting on the host country
senses.definitionCN: 驻外机构的日常职责，从签证面谈到对驻在国的情势汇报
senses.example: His first year of diplomacy was spent processing visa files.
senses.exampleCN: 他外交生涯的第一年都在处理签证档案。
senses.why: The grand word covers the paperwork of a mission, and that is where most of the work actually happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个宏大的词也涵盖驻外机构的文书工作，而大部分实际工作正发生在这里。

senses.title: Shuttle and multilateral diplomacy
senses.definition: named modes of the craft, such as a mediator travelling between capitals or many states bargaining in one forum
senses.definitionCN: 指这门技艺的特定模式，如斡旋者往返各首都，或许多国家在同一场合谈判
senses.example: Shuttle diplomacy produced a ceasefire after three weeks of flights.
senses.exampleCN: 经过三周的飞行往返，穿梭外交促成了停火。
senses.why: Modern practice developed repeatable formats, and the noun attaches to each format as a named method.
senses.whyCN: 现代实践发展出可重复的形式，这个名词便附着于每一种有名称的方法。

senses.title: Diplomacy as an instrument of policy
senses.definition: the use of envoys, aid, culture and sanctions as a softer alternative to military pressure
senses.definitionCN: 把使节、援助、文化与制裁当作军事压力之外的较软替代手段来使用
senses.example: The budget treated diplomacy as a cheaper defence than another brigade.
senses.exampleCN: 该预算把外交视为比再添一个旅更便宜的防务。
senses.why: Governments began to count influence as a resource, so the noun turned into a tool listed beside armies.
senses.whyCN: 各国政府开始把影响力当作一种资源来计算，这个名词于是变成与军队并列的工具。

senses.title: A figurative strategy of relations
senses.titleCN: 比喻：任何团体中的交际策略
senses.definition: a loosened use for the handling of alliances, rivals and feelings inside a company, family or club
senses.definitionCN: 较松散的用法，指在公司、家庭或俱乐部内部处理盟友、对手与情绪的方式
senses.example: Office diplomacy decided who would sit near the new director.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室里的交际策略决定了谁会坐在新主管旁边。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the shape of many parties, limited goods and face-saving, which any group reproduces.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了多方、有限资源与顾全面子的结构，而任何团体都会重现这一结构。

intro.en: Diplomacy reaches English through French diplomatie, a noun built on diplomatique, which goes back to Latin diploma and Greek diploma, 'a paper folded in two'. It is not a direct 'diploma plus -cy' coinage. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: diplomacy 经法语 diplomatie 进入英语；diplomatie 是在 diplomatique 基础上构成的名词，而 diplomatique 可追到拉丁 diploma 与希腊 diploma「对折的纸」。它并非「diploma 加 -cy」的直接构词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Diploun 'to fold' comes from diploos 'twofold', giving the physical image of a sheet folded once.
items.cn: diploun「折」源自 diploos「双重的」，给出了一张纸对折一次的物理意象。

items.en: The noun named a folded paper and later the letter an envoy carried to prove his commission.
items.cn: 这个名词指对折的纸，后来指使节随身携带、用以证明委任的信函。

items.en: Latin used diploma for official documents and travel warrants, the paper that opened doors for an envoy.
items.cn: 拉丁用 diploma 指官方文书与旅行许可，正是这份纸为使者打开了门。

items.en: French coined diplomatie in the eighteenth century from diplomatique, naming the business that envoys carried on.
items.cn: 法语在十八世纪由 diplomatique 造出 diplomatie，命名使节所从事的那项业务。

items.en: English borrowed the French noun for the conduct of state relations and later extended it to tact in any setting.
items.cn: 英语借入这个法语名词，指处理国家关系的行为，后又扩展到任何场合中的分寸。

items.en: Source uncertain (dates and details): the first English use is dated only approximately, and the precise path by which the credential sense became the craft sense is not fully documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（年代与细节）：英语首见年代只有约数；从「凭证」义转为「技艺」义的确切路径也缺乏完整书证。

note.en: Group one holds same-root words that look alike and name different pieces of the same field; group two holds near synonyms that differ in whether they mean an activity, a method or a personal quality.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、外形相近却指同一领域不同部分的词；第二组是近义词，区别在于指活动、方法还是个人品质。

entries.definition: An official who practises the craft; the noun names a person, while diplomacy names the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指从事这门技艺的官员；这个词命名人，而 diplomacy 命名活动。

entries.definition: The adjective of the field and of tact; it describes, while diplomacy names.
entries.definitionCN: 是该领域与分寸的形容词；它作描述，而 diplomacy 作命名。

entries.definition: The folded document or a certificate of study; it is a thing, not a practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指对折的文书或学业证书；它是一件东西，不是一种实践。

entries.definition: The scholarly analysis of old official documents, a separate discipline with its own methods.
entries.definitionCN: 指对古代官方文书的学术分析，是一门有自身方法的独立学科。

entries.definition: The whole art of managing a state, including domestic policy; diplomacy is its external branch.
entries.definitionCN: 指治理国家的整体技艺，包括内政；diplomacy 是其对外分支。

entries.definition: The specific process of bargaining toward a deal; diplomacy may include negotiation but also representation and ceremony.
entries.definitionCN: 指为达成交易而讨价还价的特定过程；diplomacy 可含谈判，但也含派驻与礼仪。

entries.definition: The personal knack of not giving offence; it is one ingredient of diplomacy, not the whole craft.
entries.definitionCN: 指不冒犯他人的个人本领；它是外交的一项成分，而非全部技艺。

entries.definition: A government's stated goals abroad; diplomacy is one of the means used to pursue them.
entries.definitionCN: 指一国政府对外宣称的目标；diplomacy 是实现这些目标的手段之一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root image is a paper folded once: the credential that let an envoy speak, and the trade that grew around it.
normal.cn: 词根意象是一张对折的纸：它让使节得以开口，围绕它长出了一门行业。

normal.en: The family runs diploma, diplomat, diplomacy, diplomatic, diplomatically, undiplomatic.
normal.cn: 同族词依次是 diploma、diplomat、diplomacy、diplomatic、diplomatically、undiplomatic。

normal.en: Fixed collocations mark the modes: quiet diplomacy, shuttle diplomacy, public diplomacy, multilateral diplomacy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各种模式：静默外交、穿梭外交、公共外交、多边外交。

normal.en: The abstract noun covers both the institution and the skill, which is why it can mean a ministry's work and a dinner-table grace.
normal.cn: 这个抽象名词同时涵盖机构与技艺，因此既能指一个部的工作，也能指饭桌上的得体。

normal.en: Near words split by role: statecraft governs, negotiation bargains, tact soothes, foreign policy aims.
normal.cn: 近义词按角色分工：statecraft 治理，negotiation 讨价，tact 安抚，foreign policy 设定目标。

abstract.en: Picture two chairs facing each other across a table, neither pushed back.
abstract.cn: 想象两把椅子隔着桌子相对，两把都没有被推开。

abstract.en: Picture one folded note passed from hand to hand until the crease wears soft.
abstract.cn: 想象同一张对折的便笺在几双手之间传递，折痕被磨得发软。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge laid plank by plank, each plank one more round of talks.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥一块板一块板地铺成，每块板就是又一轮会谈。

examples.en: Years of patient diplomacy finally produced a border agreement.
examples.cn: 多年的耐心外交终于促成了一份边界协议。

examples.en: Sanctions without diplomacy rarely change a government's mind.
examples.cn: 没有外交配合的制裁很少能改变一个政府的想法。

examples.en: She handled the family quarrel with the diplomacy of a seasoned envoy.
examples.cn: 她以老练使节般的外交手腕处理了这场家庭争吵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「diplo（对折）+ macy（办事）」——纸能对折，话能转弯 → 外交；手腕

root: 希腊 diploma「对折的纸」源自 diploun「折」，经拉丁 diploma「公文、通行凭证」进入法语 diplomatique；法语再以 diplomatique 构成名词 diplomatie，英语借入为 diplomacy。它并非「diploma 加 -cy」的直接构词；圆融义为后起引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one craft: a folded credential lets an envoy speak, and that speaking becomes a daily practice, a career, a negotiating skill, a household tact, an embassy routine, named modes, a policy tool, and finally any group's private strategy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一门技艺展开：一份对折的凭证让使节得以开口，这种开口再成为日常实务、一种职业、谈判技艺、家庭中的分寸、使馆例行工作、有名称的模式、政策工具，最后是任何团体内部的交际策略。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two parties kept at one table by talk alone, with a folded credential lying between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两方仅靠谈话被留在同一张桌边，中间放着一份对折的凭证。

branches.en: ACTIVITY AND CAREER: the daily conduct of relations and the service that carries it out are one practice seen as work and as profession (S1, S2).
branches.cn: 实务与职业：日常的关系处理与执行它的部门，是同一实践作为工作与作为职业的两面（义项一、二）。

branches.en: SKILL AT TWO TABLES: bargaining across a treaty and sparing a colleague's feelings use the same craft at different stakes (S3, S4).
branches.cn: 两种桌上的技艺：隔着条约讨价与顾全同事的感受，是同一种本事在不同赌注下（义项三、四）。

branches.en: POST AND METHOD: visa files in an embassy and a mediator flying between capitals are the routine and the named modes of one service (S5, S6).
branches.cn: 驻馆与方法：使馆里的签证档案与往返各首都的斡旋者，是同一项工作的日常与有名称的模式（义项五、六）。

branches.en: INSTRUMENT: once counted against brigades, the craft becomes a line in a defence budget (S7).
branches.cn: 工具：一旦与旅级部队相提并论，这门技艺就成了防务预算里的一行（义项七）。

branches.en: METAPHOR: any office or family repeats the table, the limited goods and the face-saving in miniature (S8).
branches.cn: 比喻：任何办公室或家庭都以缩小的规模重演这张桌子、有限资源与顾全面子（义项八）。

intro.en: Diplomacy is a French abstract noun sitting on an adjective that sits on a Greek noun of folded paper; the endings, not a '-cy' added to 'diploma', carry the abstraction.
intro.cn: diplomacy 是法语抽象名词，其下是形容词，再下是希腊「对折纸」名词；抽象义由词尾承担，而非在 diploma 后加 -cy。

latinIntro.en: Greek diploma gives the noun, Latin diplomaticus the adjective, and French -ie turns that adjective into the name of the craft.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 diploma 提供名词，拉丁 diplomaticus 提供形容词，法语 -ie 再把这个形容词变成技艺的名称。

items.example: The physical act of folding is the oldest layer of the word.
items.exampleCN: 折叠这一物理动作是这个词最古老的一层。

items.structure: diploma, diplomatis (Greek noun, later Latin noun)
items.meaning: a folded paper; an official document
items.example: The credential is a folded sheet before it is a profession.
items.exampleCN: 在成为一门职业之前，这份凭证先是一张对折的纸。

items.example: The suffix turns the document into an adjective of its field.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把文书变成该领域的形容词。

items.meaning: relating to envoys and state papers
items.meaningCN: 与使节和国家文书相关的
items.example: The adjective is the bridge between paper and practice.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是纸页与实践之间的桥。

items.example: French gave the Latin adjective its modern shape.
items.exampleCN: 法语赋予这个拉丁形容词现代形态。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into the name of a business.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成一项业务的名称。

items.example: French coined the noun before English borrowed it.
items.exampleCN: 法语先造出这个名词，英语随后借入。

items.example: English kept the French ending almost unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 英语几乎原样保留了法语词尾。

items.example: The person noun was cut back from the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个指人的名词由形容词逆构而来。

latinEntries.meaning: an official document, a letter of recommendation

latinEntries.structure: diplomaticus, diplomatica, diplomaticum (adj., first and second declension)

definition_zh: 粗鲁无礼的；愚钝的；低俗的；粗糙的
definition_en: so insensitive, stupid or vulgar as to show a lack of thought or feeling
core_image: 在葬礼上有人大声谈股票，笑声穿过黑衣人群
scene: 追悼会还没结束，就有人开始讨论遗产怎么分。 The remark was crass even by his standards.
sceneCN: 这里 crass 指全然不顾场合与他人感受的粗鲁（第 1 个义项：粗鲁无礼）；句意为这句话按他自己的标准也算粗鲁。

senses.title: Insensitive to other people
senses.definition: showing no awareness of other people's feelings or the occasion
senses.definitionCN: 对他人感受或场合毫无体察
senses.example: The remark was crass even by his standards.
senses.exampleCN: 这句话按他自己的标准也算粗鲁。
senses.why: The Latin adjective meant 'thick' or 'solid'; a thick skin cannot feel the fine grain of a situation.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁形容词意为「厚实的、结实的」；厚皮感受不到情境的细纹。

senses.title: Vulgar in taste
senses.definition: showing poor and ostentatious taste
senses.definitionCN: 品味拙劣而炫耀
senses.example: The lobby was decorated with crass gold ornaments.
senses.exampleCN: 大堂里装饰着俗气的金色饰件。
senses.why: Thickness in the eye becomes coarseness in taste: nothing subtle survives the display.
senses.whyCN: 眼中的「厚」变成品味上的「粗」：在这样的展示里，细腻的东西都活不下来。

senses.title: Grossly materialistic
senses.definition: valuing money and display above all else
senses.definitionCN: 把金钱与炫耀看得高于一切
senses.example: Critics called the campaign crass commercialism.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称这场活动是庸俗的商业主义。
senses.why: A thick desire for gain blunts every finer motive, so the word judges the appetite behind the display.
senses.whyCN: 对获利的厚实欲望磨钝了所有更精细的动机，因此这个词评判的是展示背后的胃口。

senses.title: Blatantly tactless
senses.definition: stated or done so openly that it cannot be excused as a slip
senses.definitionCN: 说得或做得过于露骨，无法以无心之失开脱
senses.example: It was a crass attempt to profit from the disaster.
senses.exampleCN: 那是借灾难牟利的露骨企图。
senses.why: Tact depends on a thin awareness of context; crassness is that awareness missing altogether.
senses.whyCN: 得体依赖于对情境的细微觉察；粗鲁则是这种觉察完全缺席。

senses.title: Coarse in texture, in old use
senses.definition: in older texts, literally thick, coarse or solid in texture
senses.definitionCN: 在较早文本中，字面指质地厚、粗或结实
senses.example: The old grammarian described the stone as crass and heavy.
senses.exampleCN: 那位古代语法学家称这块石头粗糙而沉重。
senses.why: The physical sense is the root: what is thick cannot be penetrated by light or feeling.
senses.whyCN: 物理义是根：厚实之物无法被光或感受穿透。

senses.title: Grossly stupid
senses.definition: so foolish that the stupidity seems wilful
senses.definitionCN: 愚蠢到仿佛是有意为之
senses.example: It was a crass mistake to ignore the warning.
senses.exampleCN: 无视警告是个愚不可及的错。
senses.why: Stupidity becomes crass when it could have been avoided by the simplest attention.
senses.whyCN: 当只需最简单的留心就能避免时，愚蠢就变成「愚不可及」。

senses.title: Ignorant disregard
senses.definition: a blunt refusal to learn or consider what is obvious to others
senses.definitionCN: 生硬地拒绝了解或考虑他人眼中显然的事
senses.example: His crass ignorance of the local customs offended the hosts.
senses.exampleCN: 他对当地习俗的愚钝无知冒犯了主人。
senses.why: Ignorance can be innocent, but crass ignorance is thick on purpose: it will not let information in.
senses.whyCN: 无知可以是无辜的，但 crass ignorance 是有意地厚实：它不让信息进入。

senses.title: Thick-headed in old medicine
senses.definition: in old physiology, having a thick or dull constitution
senses.definitionCN: 在旧时生理学中，指体质厚钝
senses.example: Old writers blamed a crass humour for slow wit.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时作者把迟钝的才思归咎于粗厚的体液。
senses.why: The last sense records an old theory of temperament; the metaphor of thickness survived after the theory died.
senses.whyCN: 最后一个义项记录了旧的性情理论；理论消亡之后，「厚」的比喻仍然活着。

intro.en: Crass comes from a Latin adjective meaning thick or solid, and thickness became the image for a mind that lets nothing fine through.
intro.cn: crass 来自一个表示「厚实、结实」的拉丁形容词，而「厚」成了「什么细腻之物都透不进去的心智」的意象。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the 17c. for coarse matter, then applied it to coarse manners.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个形容词，指粗糙的物质，随后用于粗鲁的举止。

items.en: Latin crassus meant 'thick, solid, fat', used of soil, air and bodies alike.
items.cn: 拉丁语 crassus 意为「厚的、结实的、肥的」，土壤、空气与身体都可以用它形容。

items.en: Crassitudo named thickness itself, a quality one could measure rather than judge.
items.cn: crassitudo 命名厚度本身，是一种可以测量而非评判的性质。

items.en: The move from thick matter to thick wit happened in English: a dense substance became a dense mind.
items.cn: 从「厚的物质」到「厚的心智」的转变发生在英语中：致密的实体变成了迟钝的头脑。

items.en: Today the word is almost always a judgement of taste or tact rather than a description of texture.
items.cn: 今天这个词几乎总是对品味或得体的评判，而不是对质地的描述。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the crass stem; the near-meaning group names kinds of coarseness.
note.cn: 形近组共享 crass 词干；近义组列出粗俗的各种形态。

entries.definition: in an insensitive or vulgar way.
entries.definitionCN: 以粗鲁或低俗的方式。

entries.definition: the quality of being insensitive or vulgar.
entries.definitionCN: 粗鲁或低俗的性质。

entries.definition: more insensitive or vulgar.
entries.definitionCN: 更粗鲁或更低俗的。

entries.definition: the most insensitive or vulgar.
entries.definitionCN: 最粗鲁或最低俗的。

entries.definition: saying or doing things without sensitivity to others.
entries.definitionCN: 说话做事不顾他人感受。

entries.definition: lacking refinement in taste or manners.
entries.definitionCN: 品味或举止缺乏修养。

entries.definition: awkward and unsure in social situations.
entries.definitionCN: 在社交场合笨拙而不自在。

entries.definition: unable or unwilling to understand what is clear.
entries.definitionCN: 无法或不愿理解明显之事。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a loud remark in a silent room.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「安静房间里突然一句大声的话」这一画面留住。

normal.en: Crass means thick: a thick hide feels nothing, and a crass remark feels nothing either.
normal.cn: crass 意为厚：厚皮什么都感觉不到，粗鲁的话也什么都感觉不到。

normal.en: Picture a joke told at a funeral, and the silence that follows.
normal.cn: 想象在葬礼上讲了个笑话，随后的一片沉默。

normal.en: The Latin crassus described thick soil; thick manners grow in the same ground.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 crassus 描述厚实的土壤；粗鲁的举止也长在同样的土里。

normal.en: Say KRASS, one hard syllable, like a blunt object landing.
normal.cn: 读成 KRASS，一个硬邦邦的音节，像钝器落地。

normal.en: Link it with tactless: both describe a missing filter.
normal.cn: 把它和 tactless 联系：两者都描述缺失的过滤。

abstract.en: What is thick cannot be penetrated by nuance.
abstract.cn: 厚的东西无法被细微之物穿透。

abstract.en: Crassness is not ignorance of the rule but indifference to it.
abstract.cn: 粗鲁不是不知道规则，而是对规则漠不关心。

abstract.en: A single crass remark can reveal a whole way of seeing.
abstract.cn: 一句粗鲁的话，就能暴露一整套看世界的方式。

examples.en: The remark was crass even by his standards.
examples.cn: 这句话按他自己的标准也算粗鲁。

examples.en: Critics called the campaign crass commercialism.
examples.cn: 批评者称这场活动是庸俗的商业主义。

examples.en: His crass ignorance of the local customs offended the hosts.
examples.cn: 他对当地习俗的愚钝无知冒犯了主人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「厚」：脸皮厚、感觉钝，什么都透不进去，就是「粗鲁、愚钝」。

root: 拉丁语 crassus（厚的、结实的）

sensesIntro.en: Crass always describes a thickness that blocks feeling or understanding; the senses differ in whether what is blocked is tact, taste, thought or texture.
sensesIntro.cn: crass 始终描述一种阻断感受或理解的「厚」；各义项的差别在于被阻断的是得体、品味、思考还是质地。

core.en: THICK AND IMPENETRABLE
core.cn: 厚实而不可穿透

branches.en: Failure to feel or to learn what others see.
branches.cn: 感受不到或学不会他人看得见的东西。

branches.en: Vulgar display and greed rather than subtlety.
branches.cn: 低俗的展示与贪婪，而非细腻。

branches.en: Tactlessness so open it cannot be excused.
branches.cn: 露骨到无法开脱的不得体。

branches.en: The old literal sense of coarse texture.
branches.cn: 质地粗糙的古老字面义。

branches.en: Stupidity and the old theory of a dull constitution.
branches.cn: 愚钝，以及旧时关于迟钝体质的理论。

intro.en: The family is small: an adverb, a noun and two comparison forms, all carrying the same judgement.
intro.cn: 这个词族很小：一个副词、一个名词和两个比较形式，都带着同一种评判。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root describes thickness in soil and body; English moved the thickness into manners.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根描述土壤与身体之厚；英语把这种厚搬到了举止上。

items.meaning: in a manner that shows no tact
items.example: He crassly asked about her salary.
items.exampleCN: 他粗鲁地打听她的薪水。

items.example: The crassness of the joke silenced the room.
items.exampleCN: 那个玩笑的粗俗让全场安静。

items.example: The second ad was even crasser.
It was the crassest thing he had ever said.
items.exampleCN: 那是他说过的最粗俗的话。

items.example: Critics mocked the crassitude of the plot.
items.exampleCN: 批评者嘲弄情节的粗笨。

items.example: The wedding became a display of crass materialism.
items.exampleCN: 婚礼成了一场粗鄙拜金的展示。

items.example: The holiday was buried under crass commercialism.
items.exampleCN: 这个节日被庸俗的商业主义掩埋了。

items.example: He told a crass joke and lost the room.
items.exampleCN: 他讲了个低俗玩笑，失去了全场。
